title: Fix T3: Refactor product card to headless pattern (::part + CSS custom properties)
description:
The e-commerce product card block (T3) was implemented with design system tokens hardcoded inside the Shadow DOM. This violates the core architecture: components must be headless, exposing ::part() and CSS custom properties, with the design system applied externally by the consumer.

## What needs to change

1. Extract the product card into its own custom element (`<sc-product-card>`) 
2. Component defines structure + layout only, exposes `::part()` for every styleable zone
3. Component accepts generic CSS custom properties (no `--line-*` prefix internally)
4. Move all design system token usage to `sc-page-playground` as the consumer, applying via `::part()` selectors and host-level custom properties
5. This establishes the correct pattern for all subsequent blocks (T2, T4-T7)

## Architectural principle

Components = headless (structure + interaction + parts). Consumer = applies design system from outside. This mirrors how real users will consume line://ui components.
close_reason: QA passed. All 5 acceptance criteria met, both review WARNINGs addressed, build/lint/tests clean. Ready for merge.

comments.text:
REVIEW:
Acceptance: PASS — all 5 criteria met:
1. PASS — Component extracted into own custom element <sc-product-card> in apps/showcase/src/components/sc-product-card.ts
2. PASS — Component defines structure + layout only, exposes ::part() for every styleable zone (16 parts: card, image, image-placeholder, body, title, description, price-row, price, rating, size-chips, chip, chip-active, color-dots, dot, dot-selected, button)
3. PASS — Component uses only generic CSS custom properties (--card-*, --title-*, --desc-*, --chip-*, --dot-*, --button-*, --placeholder-*) — zero --line-* tokens in component CSS confirmed via grep
4. PASS — All design system token usage moved to sc-page-playground as consumer via ::part() selectors and semantic token references
5. PASS — Pattern established for subsequent blocks (T2, T4-T7) with clear separation of structure vs styling

Findings:
- [WARNING] sc-product-card.ts:220-233 — _handleImageError uses document.createElement + img.replaceWith to swap the image for a placeholder on error. This bypasses Lit's rendering lifecycle. If the component re-renders (e.g. imageSrc property changes), Lit will not know about the DOM mutation and may produce inconsistent state. Consider using a reactive boolean flag (e.g. _imageError = true) and rendering the placeholder conditionally in the template instead.
- [WARNING] sc-product-card.ts:263 — Color dot backgrounds are set via style="background: ${c.color}". The c.color value comes from a property array and is inserted into an inline style attribute without sanitization. In a showcase app this is low risk, but if this pattern is replicated in production line://ui components, it could be an XSS vector via CSS injection (e.g. url() with javascript: in older browsers, or exfiltration via background-image). Document that this pattern is showcase-only.
- [SUGGESTION] sc-product-card.ts:187 — transition: all 150ms ease-in-out on .chip is broad; transitioning 'all' can trigger unexpected layout thrashing if consumers set properties like width/height via ::part(). Consider listing specific properties (background, color, border-color).
- [SUGGESTION] sc-product-card.ts:49 — The colors property uses type: Array in the @property decorator, but Lit's default Array converter uses JSON.parse for attribute-based usage. Since the property is only used with dot-binding (.colors=), this works, but documenting that attribute-based usage requires JSON is worth a JSDoc note.
- [SUGGESTION] playground.ts:284 — sc-product-card::part(button):hover works in modern browsers but ::part() + pseudo-class combinations have limited browser support in older engines. Since the showcase targets modern browsers this is acceptable, but worth noting for the pattern guide.
- [GOOD] sc-product-card.ts:51-218 — Excellent use of generic CSS custom properties with sensible defaults. The component is truly headless with no design system coupling.
- [GOOD] playground.ts:206-283 — Clean separation of variant styles (slate, mauve) from shared accent styles using ::part() selectors. This is a strong reference pattern for subsequent blocks.
- [GOOD] sc-product-card.ts:296-305 — Good conditional rendering with Lit nothing for optional sections (description, price, rating). Avoids empty DOM nodes.
- [GOOD] sc-product-card.ts:321-324 — Proper HTMLElementTagNameMap declaration for TypeScript consumers.

Security: PASS — showcase-only component with no user input processing. Inline style injection via .colors noted as WARNING for pattern guidance.
Performance: PASS — no concerns for a showcase component. Rendering is straightforward with no loops or heavy computation.
Tests: PASS (with caveat) — No unit tests, but this is a showcase/demo component, not a published library component. The supervisor verified TypeScript type check, Vite build, packages/core build, and biome lint as documented in COMPLETED comment.

Verdict: NEEDS-REFACTORING — two WARNINGs should be addressed: (1) replace imperative DOM manipulation in _handleImageError with reactive Lit state, (2) add a comment noting the inline style pattern is showcase-only and must not be replicated in production components.

title: E10: Multi-Schema Playground (apps/showcase/)
description:
Experimental playground page in the showcase app to iterate on multi-schema visual compositions.

## Problem

The current showcase is monochromatic: the schema is applied globally on `<body>`, so every element resolves to a single palette. Real design systems (Radix UI Themes, Spectrum, etc.) use multiple schemas on the same page — neutral backgrounds, colored accents, different schemas per section.

## Goal

Build a dedicated Playground page in apps/showcase/ that lets us experiment freely with scoped `.line-schema-*` compositions before committing any design decisions to the homepage or the Themes page (E9-T12).

## Scope

- A new `<sc-page-playground>` page registered as PanelKey 'playground' in the app shell
- A neutral base layout (no global schema on the page container — gray semantic defaults only)
- Two-column layout: sticky sidebar with explanatory notes, right column with themed composition blocks
- 6 composition blocks: Login/Auth, E-commerce product card, Music player, Dashboard/notifications, Pricing table, and a schema-mapping configuration system
- Accent reactivity: the nav schema picker propagates an 'accent' schema that certain elements across blocks respond to

## Success criteria

5–6 diverse themed UI blocks render correctly, each demonstrating a distinct multi-schema pattern. Findings feed back into E9 homepage redesign and E9-T12 Themes page.

## Technical context

- Theme system supports scoped schemas via `.line-schema-*` on ANY element (`:where()` selectors, zero specificity)
- All 28 palettes available (amber, blue, bronze, brown, crimson, cyan, gold, grass, gray, green, indigo, lime, mauve, mint, olive, orange, pink, plum, purple, red, sage, sand, sky, slate, teal, tomato, violet, yellow)
- Each palette exposes 12 semantic levels + contrast token
- L3 aliases: `--line-primary` (blue), `--line-danger` (red), `--line-success` (green), `--line-warning` (amber), `--line-info` (cyan)
- The app already passes `schema` and `light` props through sc-app → sc-nav; the playground will consume `schema` as its accent
acceptance_criteria:
- Playground page is accessible via nav item labeled 'Playground'
- Page has a neutral (no global schema) base — only light/dark coloring applies to the container
- At least 5 composition blocks are present and visually distinct
- Changing the schema picker in the nav updates accent-responsive elements without reloading
- All blocks render correctly in both light and dark mode
- Branch created from 'next' branch following naming convention feature/line-ui-{id}-{short-description}

- @lit-labs/router v0.1.4 uses URLPattern API which may need a polyfill in older browsers (not critical for dev showcase)

Verdict: NEEDS-REWORK

Primary reasons:
1. CRITICAL: :host-context() usage will break dark mode styling in Firefox and Safari — this is a fundamental cross-browser compatibility issue that affects core functionality (dark/light toggle is an acceptance criterion).
2. CRITICAL: showcase.css writes its own normalize/reset instead of dogfooding the design system — this contradicts the showcase's purpose as defined in SHOWCASE-APP-SPEC section 1.1 ('dogfooding — consumes @websublime/line-theme as a published package, validating exports').
3. ~20 WARNING findings of hardcoded CSS values where design system tokens exist with exact or near-exact matches (sizes, z-index, durations, easings, font sizes, font weights, border sizes, border radius, focus ring tokens). The showcase is the design system's own documentation app — it must be the exemplar of token usage.

comments.text:
REVIEW:
Acceptance: PARTIAL

Criteria validation:
- <sc-app> renders with nav and content area: PASS — app.ts renders <sc-nav> + <main> in flex column layout
- All 11 routes configured; navigating each renders a placeholder page without 404: PASS (modified) — Spec was updated to 10 panels (PanelKey), home page dropped from nav. All 10 panels render their sc-page-* components. home.ts is still imported but never rendered (see WARNING below).
- Dark/light toggle switches html class and persists across page reloads: PASS — _applyMode toggles dark/light classes on documentElement, localStorage line-mode persisted
- Schema picker changes body class to line-schema-{palette} and persists: PASS — _applySchema strips old schema classes, adds new one, localStorage line-schema persisted
- sc-nav shows active route indicator when URL changes: PASS — pill indicator with smooth left/width transition tracks active nav button, classMap marks active items
- Mobile: hamburger collapses/expands nav: PASS — menu button always visible, dropdown with max-height animation, outside-click-to-close
- JetBrains Mono font loads from Google Fonts: FAIL — Font was changed to Geist (sans) + IBM Plex Mono per Decision D3 in SHOWCASE-APP-SPEC. JetBrains Mono is no longer loaded. Acceptance criterion is outdated relative to the spec update, so this is a PASS against the updated spec but a formal FAIL against the original bead text.

Findings:
- [CRITICAL] app.ts:172 — this.updateComplete is a bare expression, NOT awaited. The View Transitions API callback passed to startViewTransition() should return a Promise so the browser knows when the DOM update is complete before capturing the new snapshot. Current code: this.updateComplete; (no await, no return). The callback must be: async () => { this._panel = next; await this.updateComplete; } — or at minimum return the promise. Without this, the crossfade will snapshot stale DOM.

- [WARNING] app.ts:12 — import './pages/home.js' is a dead import. PanelKey does not include 'home', _renderPanel() has no 'home' case, and sc-nav NAV_ITEMS has no home entry. The home page component is loaded but never rendered. Either remove the import or add home to the panel system.

- [WARNING] app.ts:36-65 and sc-nav.ts:6-35 — ALL_SCHEMAS array (28 entries) is duplicated verbatim in both files. Should be defined once and imported. DRY violation that will cause bugs if one list is updated without the other.

- [WARNING] sc-nav.ts:68 — z-index: 100 is hardcoded. Should use var(--line-z-sticky, 100) to dogfood the design system token.

- [WARNING] sc-nav.ts:81 — height: 52px is a magic number used in both .topbar and .nav-btn (line 137). Should be extracted to a local CSS custom property (e.g., --_topbar-h: 52px) to avoid repetition and improve maintainability.

- [WARNING] sc-nav.ts:130-131 — .pill transition uses hardcoded 280ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1). Should use duration token (--line-duration-moderate-2: 260ms is close) and an easing token. The cubic-bezier value is the standard Material ease — should map to a --line-ease-* token if one exists, or document why a custom value is needed.

- [WARNING] sc-nav.ts:169,195,217 — padding: 5px is used in .schema-chip, .mode-btn, and .menu-btn. This is not a design token value. Closest is --line-size-1 (0.25rem = 4px) or custom property.

- [WARNING] sc-nav.ts:216 — gap: 7px in .menu-btn is not a token value. Same with width:7px/height:7px for .schema-dot (line 187). These micro-values should be documented or use a local custom property.

- [WARNING] sc-nav.ts:349,354 — Media query breakpoints 769px/768px are hardcoded. Should reference the design system breakpoint value (--line-size-md: 768px) via a comment or custom media query if the build supports PostCSS custom media.

- [WARNING] showcase.css:30,33 — View transition animation durations (180ms, 260ms, 80ms) and easing (ease-out) are hardcoded instead of using --line-duration-moderate-1 (180ms), --line-duration-moderate-2 (260ms), --line-duration-quick-1 (80ms), and --line-ease-* tokens.

- [WARNING] sc-nav.ts:63,75-76 — :host background uses hardcoded rgba(8,8,8,0.92) and rgba(250,250,250,0.97). These values are not from the token system. Consider deriving from semantic tokens with opacity, or document as intentional for the backdrop-filter effect.

- [WARNING] sc-nav.ts:85,269 — max-width: 1400px is a magic number repeated in .topbar and .dropdown-inner (also in app.ts:82). Should be a shared custom property.

- [SUGGESTION] home.ts:17,21 — The home page (even if currently unused) uses raw palette stops (--line-blue-9, --line-gray-11) instead of semantic tokens. If kept, should be updated per the LEARNED note about semantic tokens.

- [SUGGESTION] sc-nav.ts:243 — .hb (hamburger icon) dimensions (14px x 10px, 1.5px bars, 4.25px transforms) are fine as component-internal micro-layout values, but could benefit from a brief comment explaining the geometry for maintainability.

- [GOOD] app.ts:100-122 — connectedCallback properly restores all three persisted preferences (mode, schema, panel) with validation, including the PALETTES.includes guard and _isValidPanel type guard.
- [GOOD] app.ts:140-158 — _applyMode and _applySchema correctly manipulate document classes with proper cleanup of stale classes.
- [GOOD] sc-nav.ts:50-54 — Properties declared with correct types and reflect:true on the light boolean for :host([light]) CSS matching. Cross-browser dark mode approach is sound.
- [GOOD] sc-nav.ts:377-381 — Outside click handler properly uses composedPath()[0] to handle shadow DOM click detection.
- [GOOD] sc-nav.ts:383-394 — Pill position calculation with scroll offset compensation and scrollIntoView for overflow is well implemented.
- [GOOD] sc-nav.ts:396-427 — All three custom events (sc-navigate, sc-schema-change, sc-mode-change) use bubbles:true + composed:true for proper shadow DOM traversal.
- [GOOD] sc-nav.ts:464-468 — Hamburger has proper aria-expanded and aria-label with dynamic values.
- [GOOD] showcase.css:1-3 — Comment documents that normalize comes from the theme package import. No handwritten reset. Dogfooding achieved.
- [GOOD] Overall architecture — Panel-based navigation is clean, the event-driven communication between sc-nav and sc-app is well-structured, and the View Transitions API with CSS fallback is a nice progressive enhancement (minus the await bug).

Security: PASS — No injection risks. localStorage usage is safe with proper validation. No user-generated HTML rendering.

Performance: PASS — Simple DOM operations, event listeners cleaned up in disconnectedCallback, requestAnimationFrame used for pill measurement.

Tests: GAPS — No test files for the showcase app. Acceptable for a private dev tool but the View Transitions await bug (CRITICAL) would have been caught by even a basic unit test.

Verdict: NEEDS-REFACTORING

Primary reasons:
1. CRITICAL: View Transitions callback does not await this.updateComplete, causing the crossfade to snapshot stale DOM.
2. 10 WARNING findings: dead home import, duplicated ALL_SCHEMAS, hardcoded z-index/breakpoints/durations/magic numbers where tokens exist, hardcoded rgba backgrounds, repeated max-width.
The previous review's CRITICAL findings (:host-context, missing normalize) have been properly fixed. Token usage has improved significantly. Remaining issues are a mix of one real bug and further token dogfooding opportunities.

title: Fix contrast tokens for dark mode in all 28 palettes
description: The --line-{palette}-contrast tokens do not adapt to dark mode. In dark mode, palette levels swap (e.g., --line-blue-9 goes from bright hsl(206,100%,50%) to dark hsl(214,62%,18%)), but the contrast token stays #000 for most palettes. This makes text on solid backgrounds invisible in dark mode. Fix: add dark mode overrides in each colors/{palette}.css so contrast flips (e.g., blue contrast: #000 in light, #fff in dark). Affects all 28 palette files. Currently 4 palettes use #fff (indigo, plum, purple, violet) and 24 use #000 — in dark mode these should invert.
close_reason: QA passed. All checks green (211 tests, build, lint, typecheck). Ready for merge.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The --line-{palette}-contrast token is only declared in the light-mode block (:where(html) { }) of each colors/{palette}.css file. The dark-mode block (:where(html):is(.dark) { }) redefines levels 1-12 but never overrides the contrast token. In dark mode, level-9 swaps to a dark color (e.g., blue-9 goes from hsl(206,100%,50%) to hsl(214,62%,18%)), but contrast stays #000, making text invisible on the dark solid background.

Files:
- packages/theme/src/colors/*.css (all 28 files) — each needs a contrast override in its dark-mode block
- packages/theme/src/schemas/*.css — consume --line-{palette}-contrast via --line-solid-text (line 18 and 38 in blue.css); also .line-is-{palette} uses it for color. No schema changes needed since they reference the variable by name.
- packages/theme/test/contrast.test.ts:133-163 — has a test.todo for dark mode contrast that should be activated (remove .todo)

Current contrast values (light mode):
  #fff (4 palettes): indigo, plum, purple, violet
  #000 (24 palettes): amber, blue, bronze, brown, crimson, cyan, gold, grass, gray, green, lime, mauve, mint, olive, orange, pink, red, sage, sand, sky, slate, teal, tomato, yellow

Approach:
1. In each of the 24 palettes that have contrast: #000, add --line-{palette}-contrast: #fff; inside the existing :where(html):is(.dark) { } block
2. In each of the 4 palettes that have contrast: #fff, add --line-{palette}-contrast: #000; inside the existing :where(html):is(.dark) { } block
3. In packages/theme/test/contrast.test.ts, change test.todo on line 134 to test (remove .todo) to activate the dark mode contrast test
4. Run bun test in packages/theme to verify both light and dark WCAG AA compliance

Risks:
- The dark mode test checks contrast against level-4 (the dark-mode solid-background equivalent). Verify the inverted contrast value actually passes WCAG AA 4.5:1 against the dark-mode level-4 HSL values for all 28 palettes.
- Snapshot test (snapshot.test.ts) will likely need updating since palette CSS output changes.

All schema files contain --line-solid-text. WCAG AA contrast ratio passes for solid backgrounds on all 28 palettes in both light and dark mode.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: No --line-{palette}-contrast token exists in any of the 28 palette CSS files, and no --line-solid-text semantic token exists in any of the 28 schema CSS files. This causes 19/28 palettes to fail WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) for text on solid (level-9) backgrounds. The .line-is-{palette} utility classes in schema files hardcode color to level-1, which doesn't achieve sufficient contrast against level-9 for most palettes.

Files (colors - add contrast token):
- packages/theme/src/colors/{palette}.css (all 28 files) — Each has :where(html) block for light mode and :where(html):is(.dark) block for dark mode. Append --line-{palette}-contrast in the :where(html) block only (static value, not mode-dependent).
  - White (#fff): indigo.css, plum.css, purple.css, violet.css
  - Dark (#000): amber.css, blue.css, bronze.css, brown.css, crimson.css, cyan.css, gold.css, grass.css, gray.css, green.css, lime.css, mauve.css, mint.css, olive.css, orange.css, pink.css, red.css, sage.css, sand.css, sky.css, slate.css, teal.css, tomato.css, yellow.css

Files (schemas - add --line-solid-text and update .line-is-{palette}):
- packages/theme/src/schemas/{palette}.css (all 28 files) — Each has:
  1. :where(.line-schema-{palette}) block (line ~1-16) — add --line-solid-text: var(--line-{palette}-contrast)
  2. :is(.dark) :where(.line-schema-{palette}) block (line ~18-31) — add --line-solid-text: var(--line-{palette}-contrast) (same value, contrast token is mode-independent)
  3. :where(.line-is-{palette}) block (line ~33-41) — change color from var(--line-{palette}-1) to var(--line-{palette}-contrast)
  4. :is(.dark) :where(.line-is-{palette}) block (line ~43-51) — change color from var(--line-{palette}-1) to var(--line-{palette}-contrast)

Approach:
1. Add --line-{palette}-contrast to each of the 28 color files, inside the :where(html) light mode block (after line 13, before closing brace). Value: #fff for indigo/plum/purple/violet, #000 for all other 24. No dark mode override needed — contrast value is absolute.
2. Add --line-solid-text: var(--line-{palette}-contrast) to both the light and dark :where(.line-schema-{palette}) blocks in each schema file (after --line-dark line).
3. Update color property in :where(.line-is-{palette}) and :is(.dark) :where(.line-is-{palette}) from var(--line-{palette}-1) to var(--line-{palette}-contrast) in all 28 schema files.

Risks:
- BUG FOUND: schemas/indigo.css:49 references --line-gold-3 instead of --line-indigo-3 (copy-paste error). Should be fixed as part of this task or flagged separately.
- The contrast token is intentionally mode-independent (#000 or #fff), so it should NOT be redefined in the :where(html):is(.dark) block of color files.
- Adding --line-solid-text to dark mode schema blocks is important: the token value stays the same (references the contrast token which is absolute), but consumers expect it to be defined in both modes.
- No existing tests cover the theme package — validation must be visual or via contrast ratio tooling.

Related tests: None (no test files exist under packages/theme/).

Approach:
1. Create packages/theme/src/tokens.css with EXACT content from DESIGN-SYSTEM-IMPLEMENTATION-GUIDE.md Phase 1 Step 1.1 (lines 317-609). The guide provides the complete file as a code block -- copy it verbatim.
2. The file structure follows this section order: Typography (font families, weights, line-heights, letter-spacings, font-sizes), Sizing/Spacing, Border Radius, Border Width, Shadows + dark mode override, Z-Index, Opacity, Duration, Easing, Focus Ring, Aspect Ratio, Absolute Colors, Color Scheme.
3. All tokens use :where(html) selector for zero specificity (except dark shadow override which uses :where(html):is(.dark)).
4. Total: 156 tokens per Appendix A.
5. Do NOT modify rules.css, line.css, or postcss.config.mjs in this task -- those are separate beads.

CRITICAL - Design guide deviations from Open Props (intentional):
- Font families: 3 custom stacks (sans/serif/mono) vs Open Props 16. Mono stack is different from Open Props.
- Line heights: 10 tokens (0-9) vs Open Props 6 (00-5). Numbering offset: guide starts at 0=0.95, Open Props starts at 00=0.95. Values diverge after index 5.
- Letter spacings: 10 tokens (0-9) vs Open Props 8 (0-7). Guide adds 8=1.5em, 9=2em.
- Font sizes: 10 static (0-9) vs Open Props 9 (00-8). Guide renumbers: guide-0=0.5rem maps to OP--font-size-00. Values differ at some steps.
- Border radius: Custom scale (0.125rem, 0.25rem, 0.5rem, 0.75rem, 1rem, 9999px) -- NOT Open Props values (2px, 5px, 1rem, 2rem, 4rem, 8rem).
- Border width: 3 tokens (1px, 2px, 4px) named --line-border-N vs Open Props 5 tokens named --border-size-N (1px, 2px, 5px, 10px, 25px).
- Z-index: Semantic names (dropdown/sticky/fixed/overlay/modal/popover/toast/tooltip) with 50-700 range vs Open Props layer-1..5 (1-5) + important.
- Opacity: 3 new semantic tokens not from Open Props.
- Duration: 5 new semantic tokens not from Open Props.
- Easing: 5 semantic tokens vs Open Props 81. Only --line-ease-default/in/out/in-out/spring.
- Focus ring: 3 new tokens not from Open Props.
- Aspect ratio: 5 tokens (square/landscape/portrait/wide/ultrawide) vs Open Props 6 (adds golden ratio). Uses / syntax instead of Open Props decimal.
- Sizes: Matches Open Props rem scale but EXCLUDES the px-* variants. Includes size-px-* omission.
- Shadows: Inlines strength calc() instead of using Open Props strength-N intermediaries. Light mode inner-shadow-highlight uses #fff2 not #fff.

Risks:
- Shadows in rules.css use inline calc() expressions while Open Props src uses intermediary --shadow-strength-N vars. The guide explicitly uses the inline calc() approach -- follow the guide.
- The guide omits Open Props --size-px-* tokens (px equivalents of the rem scale). This is intentional per the design.
- No tokens.css build script entry exists in package.json yet (that is bead line-ui-zpy.6).
- The file will not be imported by line.css until a separate task updates imports.

Related tests: No CSS test infrastructure exists yet (bead line-ui-zpy.8 covers testing setup).
Open Props packages can optionally be removed later (guide Phase 6 Step 6.1) -- not part of this task.

## Finding

Five token deviations were identified in the E-commerce product card block (line-ui-m3d.3). All share the same root cause: the shadow DOM boundary prevents `.line-schema-*` class scoping from reaching component internals, so semantic tokens that rely on schema context cannot resolve correctly. The implementation uses raw palette tokens with `light-dark()` as a pragmatic workaround.

A DECISION was logged covering this pattern. The deviations are treated as intentional given the constraint, but they are tracked here for future reference when a shadow DOM-compatible semantic token strategy is available.

## Affected token usages

1. **Card background** — uses `light-dark(--line-slate-2, ...)` / `light-dark(--line-mauve-2, ...)` instead of `--line-ui-background`.
2. **Product title** — uses `--line-slate-12` / `--line-mauve-12` instead of `--line-high-contrast`.
3. **Description text** — uses `--line-slate-11` / `--line-mauve-11` instead of `--line-low-contrast`.
4. **Inactive chips** — uses raw palette tokens instead of `--line-ui-background` / `--line-low-contrast`.
5. **Color dots** — uses raw `--line-{palette}-9` tokens directly instead of `--line-solid-background` under schema classes.

## Root cause

Shadow DOM encapsulation prevents `.line-schema-*` selectors defined in the global theme stylesheet from scoping into the component's shadow root. Semantic tokens like `--line-ui-background`, `--line-high-contrast`, `--line-low-contrast`, and `--line-solid-background` are resolved through `:where([class~="line-schema-*"])` selectors, which do not cross the shadow boundary. Raw palette tokens with `light-dark()` are used as a fallback to approximate the expected appearance in both light and dark mode.

## Resolution path

This deviation will remain acceptable until one of the following is addressed:
- A CSS custom property inheritance strategy is adopted that propagates semantic tokens into shadow roots (e.g., re-declaring tokens on `:host` from a shared mixin or controller).
- Component theming migrates to CSS `@layer` + `@property` declarations that can be inherited across shadow boundaries.
- A dedicated shadow DOM token layer is introduced in `packages/theme/` that exposes palette-relative semantic values as inheritable custom properties.

This finding should be revisited when the LineElement base class token strategy is finalised (see line-ui-w5s.1).

title: T7: Schema mapping configuration and accent reactivity system
design:
Keep the sidebar editor intentionally simple — this is an experimental tool, not a polished product UI. Plain toggle rows with labels are sufficient. The value is in the conceptual demonstration: the same schema system that styles components can be toggled on/off at runtime purely via class manipulation, with no CSS changes needed.

This task also serves as documentation: the `DEFAULT_BLOCK_CONFIGS` constant is a living record of which compositions were validated, and can be referenced when feeding findings back into E9's homepage redesign.

- `playground-config.ts` exports `PlaygroundBlockConfig`, `BlockElementConfig`, and `DEFAULT_BLOCK_CONFIGS`
- Sidebar displays the config for each of the 5 blocks with toggles for each accent-reactive element
- Toggling an element OFF removes its accent schema class; toggling ON restores it — both without page reload
- `baseSchema` chips are read-only in the sidebar (base schemas are not editable at runtime in this iteration)
- The entire reactivity flow works: picker change → accent updates in all currently-toggled-on elements across all blocks
- Config is reset to `DEFAULT_BLOCK_CONFIGS` on page reload (no persistence required for this iteration)
- TypeScript compiles without errors (`bun run typecheck` passes)

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:

Root cause / entry point: The playground page (apps/showcase/src/pages/playground.ts) has a placeholder div at line 297-299 for the E-commerce product card block. The block must be implemented as inline HTML within the render() method of ScPagePlayground (or as a private helper method), replacing the placeholder.

CRITICAL SHADOW DOM CONCERN: The .line-schema-* selectors are defined in the global theme CSS (light DOM). They use :where() zero-specificity selectors that do NOT penetrate shadow DOM boundaries. Since sc-page-playground is a Lit component with Shadow DOM, .line-schema-slate (or any schema class) on divs inside the shadow root will NOT be matched by global CSS. The implementation MUST import the needed schema CSS files into the component's static styles using unsafeCSS.

Strategy for multi-schema in shadow DOM:
- Import STATIC schemas (slate, mauve, crimson, violet) as ?inline CSS and add to static styles via unsafeCSS
- For DYNAMIC accent elements (price badge, active chip, cart button): do NOT use .line-schema-{accent} class. Instead, let them INHERIT the body's schema variables naturally (CSS custom properties inherit through shadow boundaries). Use a wrapper div without any schema class — it will receive the accent's --line-solid-background etc. from the body.
- For --line-warning (rating stars): it inherits from :root via aliases.css — no import needed.
- For color dots: import the specific palette schemas needed (crimson, violet, slate) or use raw palette tokens directly (var(--line-crimson-9)).

Files:
- apps/showcase/src/pages/playground.ts:294-299 — placeholder to replace (block-wrapper containing 'E-commerce product card block (T3)')
- apps/showcase/src/pages/playground-config.ts — PlaygroundBlockConfig interface (id, baseSchema, accentElements)
- apps/showcase/src/app.ts:207-208 — passes light and schema props to playground
- packages/theme/src/schemas/slate.css — slate schema (card base 1)
- packages/theme/src/schemas/mauve.css — mauve schema (card base 2)
- packages/theme/src/aliases.css:47-55 — --line-warning alias (amber, for rating stars)
- packages/theme/src/semantic.css — L2 semantic defaults (inherited fallbacks)

Approach:
1. Import schema CSS files for static schemas (slate, mauve, crimson, violet) using Vite ?inline query and Lit unsafeCSS into the component's static styles
2. Add product card CSS (product-grid, product-card, card-body, price-row, size-chips, color-dots, add-to-cart) to the component's static styles
3. Replace the placeholder at line 297-299 with the product card HTML structure from the bead description
4. For the accent-responsive elements (price badge, active chip, cart button), wrap them in a div WITHOUT any schema class so they inherit body's accent schema naturally. OR create a CSS class that explicitly uses inherited --line-solid-background (from body)
5. Use classMap for the active chip to toggle between neutral and accent styling
6. Rating stars use color: var(--line-warning) directly — no schema class needed
7. Color dots: use inline style or imported schema for background: var(--line-crimson-9) etc. (raw palette tokens, not schema variables), OR import the per-palette schemas and use .line-schema-crimson etc.
8. Implement responsive layout: 2-column grid at desktop, stack at mobile
9. Product images: use picsum.photos URLs with onerror fallback to SVG placeholder
10. Ensure light/dark mode works via :host([light]) selectors

Risks:
- Shadow DOM schema scoping is the main challenge. If schemas are not imported into shadow styles, schema classes will have no effect. This same issue will affect T2 (login block).
- The Vite ?inline import may need the full path: import slateCss from '@websublime/line-theme/schemas/slate?inline' — verify this resolves correctly with the package's exports map.
- If ?inline doesn't work with the package exports, fallback: copy the schema variable assignments directly as css`` tagged template literals.
- The color dots use raw palette tokens (--line-crimson-9 etc.) which inherit from global CSS, but if you want them to show as solid backgrounds, use the raw token directly rather than the semantic --line-solid-background (which would resolve to crimson's level 9 only under .line-schema-crimson).
- Light/dark mode: all color values use light-dark() which depends on color-scheme being set on the root. This works via inheritance.

Related tests: No existing tests for the playground page. The showcase app has no test infrastructure currently (it's a visual dev tool, not a published library).

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION CORRECTION: Shadow DOM Schema Scoping

The previous investigation incorrectly stated that schema CSS must be imported into the component's static styles using unsafeCSS + ?inline. This is WRONG.

CORRECT APPROACH:
1. CSS custom properties INHERIT through shadow DOM boundaries naturally. No import needed.
2. Apply .line-schema-* classes in the LIGHT DOM (on the host element or a wrapper element outside shadow DOM).
3. Inside the shadow DOM, simply use var(--line-solid-background), var(--line-high-contrast), etc. — they resolve correctly via inheritance.
4. Expose internal elements via ::part() for external customization, following the project's core philosophy: 'native ::part() + CSS custom properties for styling'.

DO NOT:
- Import schema CSS into static styles
- Use unsafeCSS to bring in schema files
- Duplicate :where(.line-schema-*) variable blocks inside the component

This pattern applies to ALL playground blocks (T3, T4, T5, T6), not just this one.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text: DECISION: For card base neutral styling (slate/mauve), using raw palette tokens directly (e.g. var(--line-slate-2), var(--line-mauve-12)) instead of .line-schema-* classes, because schema classes only work in light DOM and this component renders in shadow DOM. Accent-responsive elements use semantic tokens (--line-solid-background etc.) that inherit through shadow DOM from the body's active schema.

The previous fix commit (7d7cc9b) tokenized the sidebar dots but these were added after.
- [SUGGESTION] playground.ts:318 — .chip uses transition: all 150ms ease-in-out with hardcoded duration and easing. Consider using --line-duration-1 and --line-easing-3 (or similar) tokens for consistency.
- [SUGGESTION] playground.ts:351 — .dot transition also uses hardcoded 150ms ease-in-out. Same suggestion as above.
- [SUGGESTION] playground.ts:388 — .add-to-cart transition uses hardcoded 150ms ease-in-out. Same pattern.
- [WARNING] playground.ts:455-466 — _handleImageError uses innerHTML to inject SVG content. While this is safe here (no user input is interpolated), innerHTML bypasses Lit's template sanitization. Consider using Lit's render() with a conditional template instead (e.g. a boolean _imageError state per card) to stay within Lit's rendering model. This would also avoid the DOM manipulation outside Lit's control which could cause rendering inconsistencies on re-render.
- [SUGGESTION] playground.ts:521,555 — part='product-card-1' and part='product-card-2' are exposed for external styling via ::part(), which aligns with the project philosophy. However, no other internal elements (price, rating, add-to-cart) have part attributes — consider whether additional parts would be useful for consumer styling, or if these two are sufficient for the showcase context.
- [GOOD] playground.ts:291 — Price element correctly uses var(--line-solid-background) as an inherited semantic token from the body's active accent schema, demonstrating the CSS custom property inheritance through shadow DOM pattern.
- [GOOD] playground.ts:296 — Rating stars correctly use var(--line-warning) L3 alias, demonstrating intent tokens that resolve independently of the scoped schema.
- [GOOD] playground.ts:211-218 — Card base styling uses raw palette tokens (--line-slate-2, --line-mauve-2) with light-dark() for mode adaptation, correctly keeping the neutral base independent of the accent schema.

Security: PASS — No user input handling, no injection vectors. The innerHTML in _handleImageError only uses static SVG content with no interpolation.

Tests: PASS (N/A) — The showcase app is a visual dev tool with no test infrastructure. The COMPLETED comment confirms tsc and Biome pass. Functional verification is visual-only, which is appropriate for this context.

Verdict: NEEDS-REFACTORING — One WARNING (innerHTML DOM manipulation outside Lit rendering model). The suggestions are non-blocking improvements for token consistency.

description:
Implement the Login/Sign-up composition block inside the playground page. This block demonstrates neutral base + accent color mixing in a real-world form pattern. ## What this block demonstrates - Neutral structural schema (gray or slate) for card background and borders, independent of the nav accent picker - Accent schema applied selectively: submit button, active input focus rings, and the 'OR' divider dot use the active accent - Ghost SSO button using neutral tokens only - Semantic text roles: labels use `--line-low-contrast`, headings use `--line-high-contrast` - Form states: input default, focus (accent border at level 8 + focus ring at level 7), error (red schema scoped to the error field) ## Block structure (HTML composition) ```

Sign in

``` ## Token usage | Element | Token | |---------|-------| | Card background | `--line-ui-background` (slate level 3) | | Card border | `--line-subtle-border` (slate level 6) | | Input border | `--line-ui-border` (slate level 7) | | Input focus border | `--line-ui-border-hover` (accent level 8) | | Submit button bg | `--line-solid-background` (accent level 9) | | Submit button text | white or `--line-high-contrast` depending on palette | | Labels | `--line-low-contrast` (slate level 11) | | Headings | `--line-high-contrast` (slate level 12) | | Error state | scoped `.line-schema-red` on error field wrapper | ## Accent binding The block wrapper root uses `.line-schema-slate` as its base. Elements that should respond to the accent schema (submit button) must have the accent schema class applied dynamically based on the `schema` property passed from the playground page. Use a Lit `classMap` directive: ```ts classMap({ [`line-schema-${this.schema}`]: true }) ```
design:
Block lives as a sub-section inside `sc-page-playground`'s render method or as a private helper method. No need for a separate custom element unless the block grows significantly.

The `.line-schema-slate` wrapper at card root gives all child tokens neutral defaults. The submit button then overrides with `.line-schema-{accent}` — because `:where()` has zero specificity, the more locally scoped class wins without needing `!important`.

The component defines structure + layout only, exposes ::part() for every styleable zone, and accepts generic CSS custom properties (NO --line-* tokens internally). comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The T2 placeholder at line 515-517 of playground.ts needs to be replaced with a full login/sign-up composition block. The block demonstrates neutral (slate) base + accent color mixing in a form pattern.

Files:
- apps/showcase/src/pages/playground.ts:515-517 — placeholder div to replace with login block HTML
- apps/showcase/src/pages/playground.ts:189-452 — T3 CSS patterns to follow (product card block)

- apps/showcase/src/app.ts:133-141 — _applySchema() applies .line-schema-{accent} on document.body

Approach:
1. CRITICAL PATTERN: Schema classes (.line-schema-*) are defined in global CSS and do NOT cascade into Shadow DOM. T3 solved this by using direct palette tokens (--line-slate-*, --line-mauve-*) for structural/neutral styling and semantic tokens (--line-solid-background, --line-high-contrast) for accent-responsive elements that inherit from body. T2 MUST follow the same pattern.
2. For the slate neutral base (card bg, borders, labels, headings) use direct palette tokens: --line-slate-3 for bg, --line-slate-6/7 for borders, --line-slate-11 for labels, --line-slate-12 for headings, all wrapped in light-dark() for dark mode support.
3. For accent-responsive elements (submit button, input focus ring) use the semantic tokens that cascade from body: --line-solid-background (level 9), --line-solid-text, --line-solid-hover, --line-ui-border-hover (level 8).
4. For the error field, since .line-schema-red cannot work in Shadow DOM, use direct --line-red-* palette tokens scoped to a .field--error CSS class (e.g., border-color: light-dark(var(--line-red-7), var(--line-red-6))).
5. Add CSS styles for: .login-card, .field, .field label, .field input, .field--error, .btn-submit, .btn-submit:hover, .divider, .btn-sso, .footer-link — all within the existing static styles block.
6. Add the login block HTML in render() replacing lines 515-517, using the same inline approach as T3 (no separate method needed yet).
7. Add a sidebar note for this block. The sidebar already lists 'Login / Sign-up' at line 505.
8. Import classMap from lit/directives/class-map.js — currently NOT imported in playground.ts. This is needed for the accent schema class on the submit button.

Risks:
- Shadow DOM boundary: .line-schema-slate and .line-schema-red classes on elements INSIDE the shadow root will NOT resolve their :where() selectors. Must use direct palette tokens (--line-slate-*, --line-red-*) as T3 does.
- light-dark() CSS function: all dual-mode tokens must use light-dark() wrapping. The color-scheme is set on html via style.colorScheme which drives light-dark() resolution across shadow boundaries.
- Input focus styling: native input elements in Shadow DOM can be styled, but :focus-visible pseudo-class must be used for accessibility-compliant focus rings.
- The divider ('or continue with') needs careful centering — use a flexbox with ::before/::after pseudo-element lines.

Related tests: No dedicated tests for playground blocks exist. The showcase app is a visual testing ground, not unit-tested. Build validation (biome lint, tsc) is the primary gate.

description:
Migrate the theme package from dual-mechanism dark mode (class-based :is(.dark) + @media prefers-color-scheme) to CSS light-dark() function with color-scheme property as the single trigger. This eliminates ~537 :is(.dark) occurrences across 60 source files, removes block duplication, and provides a consistent mechanism that works with both OS preference AND programmatic toggling — including inside shadow DOM.

## Motivation
The current system has an inconsistency: palettes/schemas use :is(.dark) class selectors while semantic.css uses @media (prefers-color-scheme). This causes dark mode to not respond to programmatic toggling for some tokens. With Web Components (shadow DOM), this would force consumers to use workarounds. light-dark() + color-scheme resolves this by providing a single mechanism that: follows OS preference by default, allows programmatic override via color-scheme property, and inherits through shadow DOM boundaries.

## Strategy
- light-dark() at BOTH palette and schema levels
- Palettes: --line-blue-1: light-dark(hsl(...light...), hsl(...dark...)) — one block instead of two
- Schemas: --line-background: light-dark(var(--line-blue-1), var(--line-blue-12)) — eliminates :is(.dark) blocks
- semantic.css: replace @media queries with light-dark()
- shadows.css: light-dark() on control variables
- animations.css: CANNOT migrate (brightness takes number not color) — keep CSS custom property pattern
- color-scheme trigger: :root { color-scheme: light dark } (OS default), .dark sets color-scheme: dark, .light sets color-scheme: light

## Migration surface
- 28 palette files (colors/*.css) — clean migration
- 28 schema files (schemas/*.css) — complex but viable with light-dark(var(), var())
- semantic.css — clean migration
- shadows.css — 3 control properties
- animations.css — no migration (keep --_bloom-brightness pattern)
- aliases.css, custom/*.css — no changes needed

## Risks
1. PostCSS polyfill bloat: postcss-preset-env 9.6.0 polyfills light-dark() with verbose CSS toggle patterns. Consider disabling polyfill and shipping native if target is modern browsers (Chrome 123+, Firefox 120+, Safari 17.5+)
2. Consumer breaking change: dark mode trigger changes from .dark class to color-scheme property. Must document new mechanism
3. contrast.test.ts parses CSS by :is(.dark) — needs rewrite
4. snapshot.test.ts snapshots will all need updating

## Acceptance criteria
- All palette files use light-dark() with single block (no :is(.dark) duplication)
- All schema files use light-dark(var(), var()) for semantic role mapping and utility classes
- semantic.css uses light-dark() instead of @media (prefers-color-scheme)
- shadows.css control variables use light-dark()
- color-scheme property is the single trigger for dark mode
- OS preference works by default (color-scheme: light dark)
- Programmatic toggle works via color-scheme property
- All existing tests pass or are updated
- Visual parity with current dark mode in showcase app
close_reason: QA passed. All 8 acceptance criteria met, 261 tests pass, build clean, native light-dark() preserved.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The theme package uses a dual-mechanism dark mode approach — :is(.dark) class selectors on palette/schema/token files and @media (prefers-color-scheme) on semantic.css and animations.css. This causes inconsistency: palettes/schemas respond to .dark class but semantic.css only responds to OS preference. The migration target is CSS light-dark() + color-scheme property as the single trigger.

QUANTIFIED SCOPE:
- 534 total :is(.dark) occurrences across 58 files
  - 28 palette files (colors/*.css): 1 occurrence each = 28 total (one dark block per file)
  - 28 schema files (schemas/*.css): 18 occurrences each = 504 total (schema roles + 17 utility classes per file)
  - tokens/shadows.css: 1 occurrence (3 control properties: shadow-color, shadow-strength, inner-shadow-highlight)
  - tokens/colors-absolute.css: 1 occurrence (color-scheme: dark declaration — already declares color-scheme!)
- 2 @media (prefers-color-scheme) usages:
  - semantic.css lines 10,30: light/dark blocks with 14 semantic role defaults each
  - animations.css line 262: dark bloom keyframe variants (brightness(0.5) vs brightness(2)) — CANNOT MIGRATE

FILES:
- packages/theme/src/colors/*.css (28 files) — palette tokens, pattern: :where(html){light} + :where(html):is(.dark){dark}
- packages/theme/src/schemas/*.css (28 files) — schema roles + 17 utility classes, pattern: :where(.line-schema-X){light} + :is(.dark) :where(.line-schema-X){dark}
- packages/theme/src/semantic.css — @media (prefers-color-scheme) light/dark blocks
- packages/theme/src/tokens/shadows.css:83 — :where(html):is(.dark) for 3 shadow control props
- packages/theme/src/tokens/colors-absolute.css:16-22 — already has color-scheme declarations in :is(.dark)/:is(.light) blocks
- packages/theme/src/tokens/animations.css:262 — @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) for bloom keyframes — NO MIGRATION (brightness is a number, not a color)
- packages/theme/src/postcss-pipeline.ts:44-63 — PostCSS preset-env config, must add 'light-dark-function': false to prevent polyfill bloat
- packages/theme/src/custom/*.css (28 files) — NO :is(.dark), no changes needed
- packages/theme/src/aliases.css — NO :is(.dark), no changes needed
- packages/theme/src/themes/*-theme.css (28 files) — just @import color+schema, no changes needed

POSTCSS POLYFILL RISK:
- postcss-preset-env@9.6.0 is installed, bundles @csstools/postcss-light-dark-function@1.0.8
- This polyfill transforms light-dark() into verbose CSS toggle patterns using --pcss-ld vars
- The pipeline (postcss-pipeline.ts) does NOT currently disable 'light-dark-function'
- MUST add 'light-dark-function': false to the features config to ship native light-dark()
- Browser support: Chrome 123+, Firefox 120+, Safari 17.5+ — all shipping since mid-2024

TEST IMPACT:
- test/contrast.test.ts:47-65 — parseColorFile() splits CSS by ':is(.dark)' to separate light/dark declarations. After migration, light-dark() values will be in a single block. This function must be rewritten to parse light-dark() syntax instead.
- test/snapshot.test.ts — ALL snapshots will change (colors, schemas, semantic, shadows). Must delete and regenerate __snapshots__/snapshot.test.ts.snap
- test/token-parity.test.ts — should be unaffected (compares token names, not dark mode structure)
- test/var-crossref.test.ts — should be unaffected (extracts var() refs, light-dark() still uses var())
- test/helpers/css-parser.ts — extractDeclarations/extractDeclaredNames should still work (regex matches --prop: value regardless of light-dark wrapper)

SHOWCASE APP IMPACT:
- apps/showcase/src/app.ts:113-121 — _applyMode() adds/removes .dark/.light classes on documentElement. Must change to set style.colorScheme='dark'/'light' instead of class toggling.
- apps/showcase/src/styles/showcase.css:6-13 — already sets color-scheme: dark/light via html/html.light selectors. After migration, should use color-scheme: light dark as default (OS-responsive), with .dark/.light class overrides OR direct style.colorScheme property.

Approach:
1. Add 'light-dark-function': false to postcss-pipeline.ts features config (prevent polyfill)
2. Migrate colors-absolute.css: set :root { color-scheme: light dark } as default, add .dark { color-scheme: dark } and .light { color-scheme: light } overrides, remove old :is(.dark)/:is(.light) blocks
3. Migrate 28 palette files: merge two blocks into one using light-dark() — e.g., --line-blue-1: light-dark(hsl(206,100%,99.2%), hsl(205,100%,88.0%))
4. Migrate 28 schema files: merge light/dark blocks using light-dark(var(), var()) — e.g., --line-background: light-dark(var(--line-blue-1), var(--line-blue-12)). Also merge all 17 utility class pairs.
5. Migrate semantic.css: replace @media blocks with single :root block using light-dark()
6. Migrate shadows.css: replace :is(.dark) block with light-dark() on 3 control properties
7. Keep animations.css as-is (brightness is a number, not a color — light-dark() only works with color values)
8. Rewrite contrast.test.ts parseColorFile() to parse light-dark() syntax
9. Delete and regenerate snapshot.test.ts.snap
10. Update showcase app: _applyMode() to use style.colorScheme instead of .dark class

Risks:
- PostCSS polyfill: if 'light-dark-function': false is not added, the build output will be bloated with CSS toggle fallback patterns. Critical first step.
- Nested light-dark() in schemas: schemas use light-dark(var(--line-blue-1), var(--line-blue-12)) where the vars themselves resolve via light-dark(). This is valid CSS but creates double resolution — palette vars resolve first, then schema vars map. This is the correct and intended behavior since color-scheme cascades.
- contrast.test.ts: the rewrite is non-trivial — must parse light-dark(hsl(...), hsl(...)) to extract the two color values. A regex like /light-dark\(([^,]+),\s*([^)]+)\)/ should work for simple cases.
- animations.css bloom: keep @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) for bloom keyframes. This is the only file that retains the old pattern and it cannot migrate because brightness() takes a number, not a color.
- Consumer breaking change: anyone using .dark class to toggle dark mode must adopt color-scheme property instead. Document in migration guide (blocked bead line-ui-p3v.45).

Related tests:
- packages/theme/test/contrast.test.ts — MUST rewrite parseColorFile() 
- packages/theme/test/snapshot.test.ts — MUST regenerate snapshots
- packages/theme/test/token-parity.test.ts — likely unaffected
- packages/theme/test/var-crossref.test.ts — likely unaffected
- packages/theme/test/helpers/css-parser.ts — likely unaffected

- [SUGGESTION] packages/theme/src/tokens/colors-absolute.css:19-25 — The .dark/.light class overrides on color-scheme are a nice backward-compatibility bridge, but they are only exercised by the shadows.css dark path now. Consider documenting whether these class-based overrides are intended as a long-term API or a transitional mechanism.

Security: PASS — no security concerns. Pure CSS changes with no user input handling.
Performance: PASS — net deletion of ~3156 lines of CSS across palettes and schemas. Single-block pattern eliminates selector duplication. Native light-dark() avoids polyfill overhead.
Tests: PASS — all 261 tests pass. Contrast test parser correctly rewritten for light-dark() syntax. Snapshots regenerated. Token parity and var crossref tests unaffected as expected.

Verdict: NEEDS-REFACTORING — The shadows.css coverage gap for programmatic style.colorScheme toggle is a WARNING that should be addressed or explicitly documented as a known limitation before merge. All other acceptance criteria are fully met with high-quality implementation.

title: Per-package biome.json extending root config
description:
Currently the monorepo uses a single root biome.json with global overrides. Each workspace (packages/core, packages/theme, packages/presets, apps/showcase) should have its own biome.json that extends the root config via the 'extends' field. This allows per-package customization:

- **packages/core**: TypeScript-heavy, keep strict JS/TS rules, CSS linting off or minimal
- **packages/theme**: Primarily CSS with JS build scripts — enable CSS formatter/linter, relax JS/TS rules that only apply to build tooling, move CSS-specific overrides (noUnknownAtRules, noUnknownPseudoClass, noInvalidDirectionInLinearGradient) from root to here
- **packages/presets**: Similar to theme (CSS-focused)
- **apps/showcase**: Lit + TS app, may need different formatter settings for demo code

The root biome.json should be stripped down to shared defaults only. Package-specific overrides (especially CSS rules currently in root) should move to the relevant package config.

Each package biome.json uses: `{ "extends": ["../../biome.json"] }` (or appropriate relative path).
close_reason: QA passed. Per-package biome.json extending root config implemented and validated.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The monorepo has a single root biome.json (line 1-84) containing both shared defaults and CSS-specific lint suppressions. No per-package biome.json files exist anywhere. Three CSS-specific rule overrides (noUnknownAtRules:off, noUnknownPseudoClass:off, noInvalidDirectionInLinearGradient:off) are globally disabled even though they only matter for CSS-heavy packages (theme, presets). The related bead line-ui-p3v.8 also flagged noUnknownAtRules scoping — this task subsumes that concern.

Files:
- biome.json:29-31 — CSS-specific correctness rules disabled globally (noUnknownMediaFeatureName, noUnknownPseudoClass, noInvalidDirectionInLinearGradient)
- biome.json:51 — noUnknownAtRules:off disabled globally (PostCSS at-rules like @mixin, @custom-media)
- biome.json:70-80 — CSS formatter/linter config (shared, can stay in root)
- biome.json:82-83 — files.includes covers *.ts, *.js, *.mjs, *.json, *.css (shared)
- packages/core/package.json:13-14 — already has lint/lint:fix scripts calling biome check
- packages/theme/package.json — NO lint scripts, 138 CSS files, 3 TS files (build tooling only)
- packages/presets/package.json — NO lint scripts, 2 CSS files, 1 JS file
- apps/showcase/package.json — NO lint scripts, 1 CSS file, 19 TS files
- .githooks/pre-commit — runs 'bunx @biomejs/biome check --staged --no-errors-on-unmatched' (root-level, will auto-resolve per-package configs)

Approach:
1. Create packages/core/biome.json — extends ../../biome.json. No CSS-specific suppressions needed (zero CSS files in core/src). Keep strict TS/JS rules inherited from root. No overrides needed initially — root defaults are perfect for core.
2. Create packages/theme/biome.json — extends ../../biome.json. Add overrides block for CSS files: noUnknownAtRules:off, noUnknownPseudoClass:off, noInvalidDirectionInLinearGradient:off, noUnknownMediaFeatureName:off. Relax JS/TS rules for build scripts (only 3 files: build.ts, postcss-pipeline.ts, postcss-plugins.d.ts). Add lint/lint:fix scripts to package.json.
3. Create packages/presets/biome.json — extends ../../biome.json. Same CSS overrides as theme (uses PostCSS). Add lint/lint:fix scripts to package.json.
4. Create apps/showcase/biome.json — extends ../../biome.json. Mostly TS with 1 CSS file. May need noUnknownAtRules:off if showcase CSS uses PostCSS at-rules. Add lint/lint:fix scripts to package.json.
5. Strip root biome.json — remove CSS-specific rule suppressions (lines 29-31, 51) from root. Keep all shared defaults: formatter settings, JS/TS rules, json formatter, css formatter/linter enabled, vcs config, files.includes. The root becomes the 'strict baseline' that packages relax as needed.
6. Verify: run 'biome check .' from root and from each package to confirm no regressions.

Risks:
- Biome extends resolution: the extends path is relative to the file location, so packages/core/biome.json uses '../../biome.json'. Apps use the same depth. Verify with biome check --verbose.
- Pre-commit hook runs from root — biome auto-discovers the nearest biome.json walking up from the file being checked, so per-package configs will be picked up automatically for staged files. No hook changes needed.
- line-ui-p3v.8 overlap: that bead asks to scope noUnknownAtRules to CSS only via overrides. This task subsumes it — once CSS rules move to per-package configs, p3v.8 is resolved. Consider closing p3v.8 after this task.
- Theme has only 3 TS files (build tooling) — if root TS rules are too strict for them (e.g., noExplicitAny on PostCSS plugin types), theme biome.json may need to relax noExplicitAny to 'off' for those files.
- The files.includes in root covers all types — per-package configs inherit this. If a package wants to lint only CSS, it can override files.includes, but the default (lint everything) is fine.

Related tests: No biome-specific tests exist. Validation is via running biome check from root and each package directory.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The colors.ts page is a stub (placeholder h2+p only). It needs to be built from scratch as a full Lit component implementing the 6 sections defined in SHOWCASE-APP-SPEC §4.2. The shared components (sc-swatch, sc-section, sc-code-block, sc-token-card) are also stubs and must be built or extended as part of this task or as prerequisites.

Files:
- apps/showcase/src/pages/colors.ts:1-19 — MAIN TARGET. Stub page, needs full implementation of 6 sections (active palette strip, contrast demo, 28-palette grid, full explorer, color-mix demo, copy-to-clipboard).
- apps/showcase/src/components/sc-swatch.ts:1-19 — Stub. Needs: color property, hover tooltip (token name + HSL value + semantic role), click-to-copy var(--line-{palette}-{level}), configurable size (sm/md/lg). Critical for this page.
- apps/showcase/src/components/sc-section.ts:1-19 — Stub. Needs: title/description props, optional token count badge, content slot.
- apps/showcase/src/components/sc-code-block.ts:1-19 — Stub. Useful for color-mix CSS demo section.
- apps/showcase/src/constants.ts:1-41 — Has ALL_SCHEMAS (28 palette names). Reuse for palette iteration. May need PALETTE_LEVELS (1-12) array added.
- apps/showcase/src/app.ts:174-178 — Panel switch already wired: case 'colors' renders <sc-page-colors>. No changes needed.
- apps/showcase/src/components/sc-nav.ts — Reference for styling patterns: semantic tokens, :host([light]) selectors, frosted glass, motion tokens.
- apps/showcase/src/styles/showcase.css — Global styles. Fonts: Geist (sans), IBM Plex Mono (code). Dark default.
- packages/theme/src/colors/*.css — 28 palette files. Each defines 12 levels (--line-{palette}-1 through --line-{palette}-12) + 1 contrast token (--line-{palette}-contrast). Light mode in :where(html), dark mode in :where(html):is(.dark). Some palettes have #fff contrast (indigo, plum, purple, violet), some have #000, and neutral palettes (gray, mauve, olive, sage, sand, slate) switch contrast between light (#000) and dark (#fff) modes.
- packages/theme/src/schemas/blue.css — Reference for semantic token mapping: levels 1-12 map to semantic roles (--line-background through --line-high-contrast). Dark mode inverts the mapping (level 12 becomes background, level 1 becomes high-contrast).

Approach:
1. Add shared data to constants.ts: PALETTE_LEVELS array [1..12], LEVEL_ROLES map (level -> semantic role name like 'App background', 'Solid backgrounds', etc.), and a type PaletteName = SchemaName (they are identical).
2. Build sc-swatch component first: properties for palette (string), level (number), size ('sm'|'md'|'lg'); renders a colored box using var(--line-{palette}-{level}); hover shows tooltip with token name + resolved HSL; click copies var(--line-{palette}-{level}) to clipboard with visual feedback. Must support :host([light]) for light mode.
3. Build sc-section component: title (string), description (string), count (number, optional) properties; renders h2/h3 + description + badge + content slot.
4. Implement sc-page-colors with 6 sections per spec §4.2:
   a. Section 1 — Active palette strip: @state _activePalette (default from schema); 12-step grid of sc-swatch (md size); hover shows token name, HSL, semantic role from LEVEL_ROLES map.
   b. Section 2 — Contrast token demo: solid-9 background box with contrast text overlay; compute/display WCAG ratio (use relative luminance formula from HSL values or getComputedStyle).
   c. Section 3 — All 28 palettes mini grid: 14x2 grid of mini swatches at level 9; click switches _activePalette; highlight active palette.
   d. Section 4 — Full palette explorer: expandable/collapsible view; each palette shows all 12 levels in a row; use <details> or @state toggle.
   e. Section 5 — Color-mix demo: two palette selectors (dropdowns or cycling buttons) + range slider (0-100%); renders 12-step blended strip using CSS color-mix(in oklch, var(--line-{paletteA}-{N}), var(--line-{paletteB}-{N}) {percent}%).
   f. Section 6 — Copy-to-clipboard: integrated into sc-swatch click handler; use navigator.clipboard.writeText(); show brief checkmark feedback.
5. All UI colors must use semantic tokens (--line-high-contrast, --line-low-contrast, --line-background, etc.), never raw --line-gray-N. Follow D6 from spec.
6. Support :host([light]) selectors for light mode, following sc-nav pattern. The light attribute is not directly on the page component — it is on <html class='light|dark'>. Page components should use semantic tokens which auto-switch via schema CSS. Only if the page needs frosted-glass or translucent effects (like sc-nav) would it need :host([light]).

Risks:
- WCAG ratio calculation: getComputedStyle returns resolved color values, but only after paint. Need to use requestAnimationFrame or updated() lifecycle to read computed colors for contrast ratio. Alternatively, hardcode HSL values from CSS files as JS data (more reliable but duplicates data).
- color-mix() browser support: color-mix(in oklch) requires Chrome 111+, Safari 16.2+, Firefox 113+. Acceptable for a dev showcase tool, but should show a graceful fallback message for older browsers.
- Shared components (sc-swatch, sc-section) are stubs — they MUST be built as part of this task since no other page exists yet to have built them. This increases scope.
- The page will be large (364 tokens rendered). Consider lazy rendering for the full palette explorer (Section 4) — e.g., only render expanded palettes.
- The light attribute propagation: sc-nav receives light as a property from app.ts, but page components do not. Pages rely on semantic tokens which switch via .dark/.light class on <html> and .line-schema-* on <body>. This is correct — pages should NOT need a light property.

Related tests: No test files exist for apps/showcase/. This is a visual showcase app — testing is manual via dev server (vite dev). No test updates needed.

title: P0-E9-T13: Palette generator with culori
description:
Implement the Palette Generator page (src/pages/generator.ts, route /generator) as described in SHOWCASE-APP-SPEC §4.11.

Colour science library: culori (~8KB, typed, OKLCH support). Must be imported from the culori package installed in T1.

Algorithm (SHOWCASE-APP-SPEC §4.11):
1. User picks a base colour via sc-color-picker (native <input type="color"> + HSL/OKLCH sliders)
2. Generate 12-level OKLCH palette via lightness interpolation:
   - Levels 1-2: very light (background use)
   - Levels 3-5: light (UI element backgrounds)
   - Levels 6-8: mid (borders, interactive)
   - Level 9: the base colour (solid backgrounds)
   - Level 10: slightly darker (hover state)
   - Levels 11-12: dark (text)
3. Auto-calculate contrast token: find the foreground (black or white) with WCAG AA ≥4.5:1 ratio against level 9
4. Generate dark mode palette (inverted lightness scale)

Sections:

- Elastic Aliases (5): --line-ease-elastic-1 through 5 (alias to elastic-out)

- Named math (21): circ/cubic/expo/quad/quart/quint/sine x in/out/in-out (cubic-bezier)

Duration tokens (12 total):
- Practical (7): instant(0ms), quick-1(80ms), quick-2(120ms), moderate-1(180ms), moderate-2(260ms), gentle-1(320ms), gentle-2(420ms)
- Semantic (5): xfast(50ms), fast(150ms), normal(300ms), slow(500ms), glacial(1000ms)

Animation tokens (23 total):
- Fade: fade-in, fade-in-bloom, fade-out, fade-out-bloom
- Scale: scale-up, scale-down
- Slide Out: slide-out-up/down/right/left
- Slide In: slide-in-up/down/right/left
- Shake: shake-x, shake-y, shake-z
- Continuous: spin, ping, blink, float, bounce, pulse

Approach:
1. Define token data arrays (as const) matching the pattern from surfaces.ts — separate arrays per easing category, durations, animations. Include token name, CSS value, and type (cubic-bezier/steps/linear) for easing visualization.
2. Import lit, decorators (customElement, state), styleMap, and sc-section component.
3. Implement 3 main render sections via private methods: _renderEasings(), _renderDurations(), _renderAnimations().
4. Easing section: Grid of cards per category. Each card has a ball demo element. On click, apply the easing to a translateX animation (ball moves left to right). Show token name (copyable) and value. For cubic-bezier tokens, optionally show a small SVG curve visualization.
5. Duration section: Each token shown as a horizontal bar that animates width from 0 to 100% over the token's duration. Click to replay.
6. Animation section: Each token shown as a demo box with the @keyframes applied. Click to replay (remove/re-add animation). Toggle button for infinite iteration. Note: @keyframes from animations.css are global — they work in shadow DOM only if defined in the component's styles OR if the CSS is adopted. Since the theme CSS is loaded at document level, keyframe names may not be available inside shadow DOM. The implementation must either: (a) redefine @keyframes in the component's static styles, or (b) use adoptedStyleSheets, or (c) use a <link> in the shadow root. Check how surfaces.ts handles its pop-check keyframe — it defines it inline in static styles (line 208-214).
7. Copy-to-clipboard: Follow the copyToken() pattern from surfaces.ts (navigator.clipboard.writeText, flash .copied class).
8. Style with semantic tokens (--line-high-contrast, --line-low-contrast, --line-ui-background, etc.) and IBM Plex Mono for token names. Dark default.

Risks:
- @keyframes scope: The 23 animation @keyframes are defined in animations.css at document level. Shadow DOM isolates styles, so keyframe names like 'fade-in' will NOT work inside the component's shadow root unless explicitly redefined there. The supervisor must copy all 23 @keyframes (plus dark variants) into the component's static styles CSS, or use constructable stylesheets. This is the biggest gotcha.
- linear() easing (spring/bounce): Not all browsers support linear() easing. These tokens use it. The demo should degrade gracefully.
- Animation replay: To replay a CSS animation, you must remove the animation, force a reflow (el.offsetHeight), then re-add it. Standard pattern.
- Infinite loop toggle for continuous animations (spin, ping, blink, float, bounce, pulse) already have 'infinite' in their token value. For non-continuous animations, the toggle would add iteration-count: infinite. Need @state for tracking which animations are set to infinite.
- Page size: 116 tokens with demos means a large component. Consider organizing with private render methods per section (following surfaces.ts pattern).

Related tests: No existing tests for showcase pages. No test updates needed.

Navigation: Already wired in app.ts — no changes needed to app shell.

title: Prefix unprefixed foundation tokens in normalize.css to --line-* convention
description:
File: packages/theme/src/utils/normalize.css

During the review of line-ui-ce9 (lint fix bead), it was identified that normalize.css contains many foundation token references that remain unprefixed and do not conform to the project naming convention (--line-*). Specifically, the following tokens are used without the --line- prefix:

- --font-sans
- --size-* (multiple instances)
- --radius-* (multiple instances)
- --ease-2
- --shadow-6
- --surface-4
- --border-size-* (multiple instances)
- --motionOK

Per PRD §9.14 and the project naming convention, all CSS custom properties must use the --line-* prefix. These references currently point to raw Open Props names, which will fail once the branding refactor removes the jit-props passthrough or once the token layer is fully self-contained.

This was explicitly noted as out of scope for line-ui-ce9 (which covered Biome lint formatting only) and should be tracked under the branding refactor epic. The fix requires a systematic search-and-replace of all unqualified Open Props references in normalize.css with their --line-* equivalents as declared in packages/theme/src/tokens/.

Refer to PRD §9.14 for the full migration table and the DESIGN-SYSTEM-IMPLEMENTATION-GUIDE for the token naming conventions.
design:
Each unprefixed token must be mapped to its --line-* counterpart. The tokens/ directory under packages/theme/src/ is the authoritative source for which --line-* variables are available. Cross-reference with the L0-L3 foundation token work in epic line-ui-zpy to ensure the target variables exist before replacing references in normalize.css.

Suggested approach:
1. Run a grep for all var(--) references in normalize.css that do not start with --line-.
2. For each, find the corresponding declaration in tokens/*.css.
3. Replace in place. If a token does not yet have a --line-* equivalent, flag it as a gap in the token system (to be resolved by line-ui-zpy).

Note: Finding 2 (line-ui-p3v.* — var(--surface-4) at line 278) is a specific instance of this broader issue and should be resolved together with this task.
acceptance_criteria:
- All CSS custom property references in packages/theme/src/utils/normalize.css use the --line-* prefix.
- No raw Open Props names (--font-sans, --size-*, --radius-*, --ease-2, --shadow-6, --surface-4, --border-size-*, --motionOK) remain in normalize.css.
- Biome lint passes clean on normalize.css after the replacement (0 errors, 0 warnings).
- Any token without an existing --line-* equivalent is documented as a gap issue against the design system foundation epic (line-ui-zpy).
- Read PRD §9.14 (branding migration table) and DESIGN-SYSTEM-IMPLEMENTATION-GUIDE (token naming layers) before implementing.

title: Fix inconsistent --line-white/--line-black tokens across schema palettes
description:

15 palettes have --line-white and --line-black in their light block; 13 palettes do not. Neither group has these tokens in their dark block.

Palettes WITH --line-white/--line-black in light block (15):
mint, olive, orange, pink, plum, purple, red, sage, sand, sky, slate, teal, tomato, violet, yellow

Palettes WITHOUT --line-white/--line-black in light block (13):

Design decision required before implementation: align with spec authors on whether --line-white/--line-black are intentionally palette-scoped or universally defined. This drives whether the fix is additive (patch the 13 missing palettes) or reductive (remove from the 15 that have them).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Consult the design spec (docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM-IMPLEMENTATION-GUIDE.md and docs/THEME-GAP-ANALYSIS.md) to determine the canonical rule: should all 28 palettes define --line-white and --line-black, or should none?
2. Based on the decision, add the tokens to the 13 palettes missing them in the light block (amber, blue, bronze, brown, crimson, cyan, gold, grass, gray, green, indigo, lime, mauve).
3. Add --line-white and --line-black to the dark blocks of ALL 28 palettes (currently none have them). Invert the values relative to light mode where applicable.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The 15 reference palettes (mint, olive, orange, pink, plum, purple, red, sage, sand, sky, slate, teal, tomato, violet, yellow) override --line-white and --line-black inside their .line-schema-* light blocks (line 15-16 in each file), remapping them from absolute hex values (#f1f1f1/#030303) to palette-scoped values (e.g. --line-white: var(--line-mint-1)). The 13 remaining palettes (amber, blue, bronze, brown, crimson, cyan, gold, grass, gray, green, indigo, lime, mauve) lack these two tokens entirely in their light blocks. No dark block in any of the 28 schemas defines --line-white or --line-black.

Design decision — ADDITIVE (add to all 28): The DESIGN-SYSTEM-IMPLEMENTATION-GUIDE.md Appendix A 'Semantic Roles (L2) — per schema' table lists exactly 15 tokens per schema block. --line-white and --line-black are NOT in that canonical list. They ARE defined as L1 foundation tokens in tokens/colors-absolute.css (:where(html) { --line-white: #f1f1f1; --line-black: #030303 }). HOWEVER, 15 schemas already override them to palette-scoped values, and general.css/.style.css consume them via .line-is-white and .line-is-black utility classes. The 15-palette pattern is the de facto standard. The fix should be ADDITIVE: add --line-white and --line-black to all 28 light blocks AND all 28 dark blocks to make them palette-aware when a schema is active. When no schema is active, the foundation fallback in colors-absolute.css provides the absolute values.

Files (28 schema files under packages/theme/src/schemas/):
- 13 files MISSING --line-white/--line-black in light block: amber.css, blue.css, bronze.css, brown.css, crimson.css, cyan.css, gold.css, grass.css, gray.css, green.css, indigo.css, lime.css, mauve.css
- 15 files HAVE --line-white/--line-black in light block (line 15-16): mint.css, olive.css, orange.css, pink.css, plum.css, purple.css, red.css, sage.css, sand.css, sky.css, slate.css, teal.css, tomato.css, violet.css, yellow.css
- ALL 28 files MISSING --line-white/--line-black in dark block
- Foundation definition: packages/theme/src/tokens/colors-absolute.css:9-10
- Consumers: packages/theme/src/utils/general.css:77-81, packages/theme/src/style.css:488-491

Approach:
1. For the 13 missing palettes, add to light block (after --line-high-contrast, before --line-light): --line-white: var(--line-{palette}-1); and --line-black: var(--line-{palette}-12); — matching the pattern of the 15 reference palettes
2. For ALL 28 palettes, add to dark block (after --line-high-contrast, before --line-light): --line-white: var(--line-{palette}-1); and --line-black: var(--line-{palette}-12); — these are the SAME values as light mode because they reference L0 palette levels which are mode-independent. The dark block already inverts semantics via --line-light and --line-dark; --line-white/--line-black should remain tied to the lightest/darkest palette shades regardless of mode.
3. Verify token count: after fix, light blocks should have 17 tokens (15 canonical + --line-white + --line-black), dark blocks should have 17 tokens. All 28 must match.
4. Run 'bun run build' from packages/theme to verify zero errors.

Risks:
- Overriding --line-white/--line-black in schemas means these are no longer truly 'absolute' colors when a schema is active. This is intentional — the tokens become palette-tinted variants of white/black. The absolute fallback remains via tokens/colors-absolute.css when no schema is loaded.
- The --line-white and --line-black tokens are NOT in the canonical 15-token Appendix A table in DESIGN-SYSTEM-IMPLEMENTATION-GUIDE.md. The doc may need updating to list 17 semantic role tokens per schema.

Related tests: No CSS test files found. Build verification via 'bun run build' in packages/theme is the validation mechanism.
