- packages/theme/src/tokens.css:1-20 -- Barrel file importing 10 token families from tokens/. Currently built as tokens.min.css but sub-files (tokens/*.css) have no individual builds.

Approach:
1. Rewrite src/build.ts to use PostCSS programmatic API: import postcss and load the config from postcss.config.mjs once.
2. Define glob discovery patterns for entry points. The directories to scan are: colors/*.css, schemas/*.css, themes/*-theme.css, custom/*-custom.css, utils/{general,media,normalize}.css (exclude mixins.css -- it's a mixin-only file, not an entry point), plus root-level files: tokens.css, semantic-defaults.css.
3. Define output naming convention map (must be backward compatible with current dist/ filenames):
   - src/colors/{name}.css -> dist/colors-{name}.min.css
   - src/schemas/{name}.css -> dist/schemas-{name}.min.css
   - src/themes/{name}-theme.css -> dist/theme-{name}.min.css (NOTE: 'themes' dir -> 'theme' prefix, and strip '-theme' suffix)
   - src/custom/{name}-custom.css -> dist/custom-{name}.min.css (NEW -- these had no individual builds before)
   - src/utils/{name}.css -> dist/utils-{name}.min.css
   - src/tokens.css -> dist/tokens.min.css
   - src/semantic-defaults.css -> dist/semantic-defaults.min.css
   - src/line.css -> dist/line.min.css (built separately as the bundle)
4. Process all discovered entries in parallel using Promise.all with a configurable concurrency limit (e.g., p-limit pattern or manual semaphore -- Bun supports top-level await).
5. Add --entry flag support for build:css:single (e.g., --entry colors/amber builds only that entry).
6. Reduce package.json scripts to: build, build:css (all entries), build:css:single (single entry via --entry flag), plus dev and typecheck.
7. Verify backward compatibility: run old build, snapshot dist/, run new build, diff. All existing outputs must match.

- src/utils/mixins.css must be EXCLUDED from entry discovery -- it contains only @define-mixin declarations, not standalone CSS. It is consumed via @import by other files.

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: No testing infrastructure exists yet. packages/theme/test/ directory does not exist. No test runner configured. No test scripts in package.json. The monorepo has no test dependencies (no vitest, jest, or bun:test config).

Files:
- packages/theme/package.json — no test script, no test deps. Add bun:test script here.
- packages/theme/src/tokens.css — barrel file importing 17 family files. Parity test must verify all families imported and each family validated independently.
- packages/theme/src/tokens/*.css (17 files) — per-family token files. Each must be validated against Open Props source (node_modules/open-props/src/props.*.css).
- packages/theme/src/colors/*.css (28 files) — palette files with 12 levels + contrast token, light/dark modes. Contrast validation target.
- packages/theme/src/schemas/*.css (28 files) — semantic role mappings per palette. var() cross-ref validation target.
- packages/theme/src/themes/*.css (28 files) — simple 2-line imports (color + schema). Snapshot targets.
- packages/theme/src/semantic.css — L2 defaults with light/dark via @media. var() references --line-white/--line-black.
- packages/theme/src/aliases.css — L3 aliases, 54 vars referencing palette tokens (6 roles x 9 variants).
- packages/theme/src/build.ts — PostCSS build script. Snapshot tests should compare dist/ output.
- packages/theme/src/postcss-pipeline.ts — PostCSS plugin chain (import, mixins, vars, nested, preset-env, custom-media, cssnano).
- node_modules/open-props/src/props.*.css — reference files for parity validation. Key mappings: props.fonts.css->typography.css, props.sizes.css->sizing.css, props.borders.css->borders.css, etc.

Token parity summary (OP count -> line count):
  borders: 29->29 (exact), sizes: 74->74 (exact), fonts: 56->61 (5 extensions), easing: 81->81 (exact), shadows: 21->17 (line inlines strength vars into calc()), zindex: 6->14 (8 semantic extensions), aspects: 6->6 (exact), animations: 23->23 (exact), gradients: 41->41 (exact), highlights: 3->3 (exact), layouts: 12->4 (line omits grid_adapt_mixin complex, keeps 4 core), svg: 3->3 (exact), durations: line-only (12), opacity: line-only (3), focus: line-only (3), colors-absolute: line-only (2).

Approach:
1. Create packages/theme/test/ directory structure.
2. Use bun:test as test runner (Bun 1.3.10 already installed, built-in test runner, zero deps needed).
3. Test suite A — Token Parity: Parse each tokens/*.css file, extract --line-* declarations. For each family, load the corresponding OP source (props.*.css), extract --* declarations. Verify 1:1 match (accounting for known extensions and intentional divergences like shadows inlining calc and layouts omitting grid_adapt_mixin).
4. Test suite B — var() Cross-Reference: Parse all CSS files, collect all var(--line-*) references. Collect all --line-* declarations. Verify every referenced var is declared somewhere. Special handling: schemas reference palette vars (--line-{palette}-N), aliases reference palette vars, semantic.css references --line-white/--line-black.
5. Test suite C — Contrast Validation: For each of 28 palettes, parse the color file. Extract hsl() values for levels 9 (solid-background) and 1/12 (text). Compute WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1 for normal text). Check --line-{palette}-contrast against level-9. Repeat for dark mode (inverted scale). Use color math (hsl->rgb->relative luminance->contrast ratio). No external deps needed.
6. Test suite D — CSS Snapshots: Build dist/ output first (bun run build), then snapshot each .min.css file. On subsequent runs, compare against stored snapshots. Use bun:test snapshot feature (toMatchSnapshot).
7. Add test script to packages/theme/package.json.

Risks:
- Contrast validation requires HSL-to-RGB conversion + WCAG luminance formula. Can be done in pure JS but must handle the sRGB gamma correction correctly.
- Snapshot tests depend on build output, so build must run before tests (or tests trigger build).
- Layouts divergence is intentional (OP grid_adapt_mixin uses * selector, line omits it). Parity tests must have an allow-list for known divergences.
- Shadows divergence is structural (OP uses intermediate --shadow-strength-N vars, line inlines calc()). Token count differs (21 vs 17) but functional coverage matches. Parity test must account for this.
- Some OP files dont map 1:1 to line files (e.g., props.fonts.css -> typography.css). Mapping table needed in test config.

Related tests: None exist yet. All test files to be created from scratch under packages/theme/test/.

Snapshots never fail because there is nothing to compare against. This defeats the purpose of regression detection.

Findings:
- [CRITICAL] packages/theme/.gitignore:25 — __snapshots__ is gitignored, making snapshot tests always pass on fresh clones. Snapshot files MUST be committed to serve as regression baselines. Remove __snapshots__ from .gitignore and commit the generated snapshot file.
- [WARNING] packages/theme/test/contrast.test.ts:79-80 — expect(PALETTES.length).toBe(28) runs at module scope inside describe() but outside test(). While bun:test permits this, it is fragile and unconventional. Wrap this in a dedicated test('discovers exactly 28 palettes', ...) block.
- [WARNING] packages/theme/test/contrast.test.ts:97-98,105-106 — Early returns after expect failures (if (!(level9Value && contrastValue)) return) silently pass the test when data is missing instead of failing. If a palette file changes format and no longer has a level-9 or contrast token, this test would pass silently. The expect().toBeDefined() guards above should be sufficient, but the early return undermines them. Consider replacing with explicit fail or removing the early return since expect already throws.
- [WARNING] packages/theme/test/snapshot.test.ts:77 — Only 6 of 28 palettes are snapshotted for colors, and only 3 for schemas/themes. While the comment says 'representative subset', any regression in the other 22 palette files would go undetected. At minimum, snapshot all 28 color files since they are the primary contrast-bearing output.
- [SUGGESTION] packages/theme/test/helpers/css-parser.ts:21 — The regex /(--[\w-]+)\s*:\s*([^;{}]+)/g may match custom property declarations inside CSS comments (e.g., /* --foo: bar */). Currently no such comments exist in the source, but a comment-stripping pre-pass would make this more robust for the future.
- [SUGGESTION] packages/theme/test/var-crossref.test.ts:40 — EXCLUDED_FILES uses basename matching (Set(['mixins.css'])). If a second mixins.css appears in a subdirectory it would also be excluded silently. Consider using full relative paths for the exclusion set.
- [SUGGESTION] packages/theme/test/token-parity.test.ts:49 — skipValueComparison is declared in FamilyConfig but never checked in any test logic. It is only used as documentation. Either implement value comparison for non-skipped families or remove the unused field to avoid confusion.

- [GOOD] packages/theme/test/token-parity.test.ts — Clean separation of family config with documented divergences. The omittedOpTokens/lineOnlyTokens allow-lists make intentional differences explicit and maintainable.
- [GOOD] packages/theme/package.json:25 — test:no-snapshot script provides a way to run non-snapshot tests without build dependency. Practical for CI fast-path.

Tests: GAPS — dark mode contrast deferred (28 .todo tests), snapshot regression detection is broken by .gitignore.

title: P0-E8-T7: Update showcase page for L0-L3 visualization
description: Expand theme index.html to show L0 primitives, L1 foundation tokens, L2 semantic defaults light/dark, L3 aliases. Interactive and comprehensive. Mandatory proof the design system works.
design:
## Showcase Page Design (React→Vanilla JS Conversion)

### Source
React prototype from Claude chat. Convert to pure vanilla JS + CSS using actual --line-* tokens.

### Architecture
- `index.html` — semantic HTML structure, dark-first (`html.dark`)
- `src/main.ts` — vanilla JS interactivity (no framework)
- `src/style.css` — theme imports at top + showcase-specific styles

### Visual Design
- Font: JetBrains Mono (Google Fonts import)
- Accent color: #c8ff00
- Dark-first aesthetic with smooth transitions
- Selection color: accent on black

### Sections (in order)

**Hero/Header:**
- line://ui wordmark with accent `://`
- L0/L1/L2/L3 breadcrumb dots
- Dark/light toggle button (dot indicator + label)
- Active theme palette picker (28 buttons, active shows solid-9 bg)

**L0 — Primitives:**
- 12-step active palette strip (hover expands swatch height)
- Level labels: bg, subtle, ui-bg, ui:hov, ui:act, s-brd, ui-brd, brd:hov, solid, sol:hov, lo-txt, hi-txt
- Hovered level detail (token name, HSL value, semantic role)
- Contrast token demo (solid-9 bg + contrast color)
- All 28 palettes mini grid (14×2, level 9, click to switch)
- Color-mix demo: 2 palette selects + range slider, 12-step blended strip using CSS color-mix(in oklch)

**L1 — Foundation Tokens:**
- 2-column grid layout
- Type scale (levels 0-9 with rendered "Ag" at each size)
- Spacing scale (--line-size-1 through 9, gradient bars)
- Border radius (6 samples: 1-5 + round, bordered squares)
- Elevation/shadows (6 levels, card with box-shadow)
- Motion/easing (5 curves: default, in, out, in-out, spring — bouncing ball animation, click to play/stop)
- Z-index stacking (8 semantic levels as bar chart)
- Duration + opacity (5 durations as bars, 3 opacity demos)

**L2 — Semantic Roles:**
- Side-by-side light/dark panels showing 12 semantic tokens with gray defaults
- Themed semantic strip (.line-schema-{palette} applied, 12 cells)
- Component preview: card with solid/outline/subtle buttons, input + checkbox

**L3 — Semantic Aliases:**
- 6 alias cards in grid (primary→blue, danger→red, success→green, warning→amber, info→cyan, neutral→gray)
- Each card: solid-9 header, subtle strip, palette dots
- Click to inspect: expands 9-token anatomy (base, hover, active, text, subtle, subtle-hover, outline, outline-hover, fg)
- Button variants row: solid/outline/subtle for each alias

**Footer:**
- line://ui branding + @websublime
- Token/palette/alias counts

### State Management (vanilla JS)
- `html.dark` / `html.light` — mode toggle
- `body.line-schema-{palette}` — active schema (existing pattern)
- `data-hovered-level` on L0 section — hover detail
- `data-selected-alias` on L3 section — expanded alias card
- CSS class toggles for easing animation play/stop
- Range input + selects for color-mix (read values, set CSS custom properties)

### CSS Token Usage
- Use var(--line-{palette}-{level}) for all colors — NO hardcoded HSL
- Use var(--line-solid-background), var(--line-ui-border), etc. for semantic roles
- Use var(--line-primary), var(--line-danger), etc. for aliases
- getComputedStyle() to read resolved values for JS-driven displays (hover detail panel)

### Constraints
- Only 6 aliases (primary, danger, success, warning, info, neutral)
- Keep style.css imports at top (tokens, semantic, themes, custom, aliases)
- JetBrains Mono from Google Fonts CDN
acceptance_criteria: Showcase page has distinct sections for L0 (primitives), L1 (foundation tokens from tokens.css), L2 (semantic defaults in light and dark mode), and L3 (aliases). Every token is visible on screen. Light/dark toggle works. Page serves as a visual contract that the full design system is wired correctly.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The exports field in packages/theme/package.json is incomplete. It currently has 5 entries (., ./reset, ./tokens, ./semantic-defaults, ./aliases) but needs granular exports for: palettes (colors/*), schemas/*, themes/*, utilities, normalize, and individual token families (tokens/typography, tokens/sizing, etc.).

Files:
- packages/theme/package.json:7-13 — Current exports field, needs expansion
- packages/theme/src/build.ts:57-67,74-108,113-143 — Build script controls dist output naming; currently uses flat naming (colors-amber.min.css) not subdirs (colors/amber.min.css)
- packages/theme/src/tokens.css:1-27 — Barrel file importing 17 token families; individual families are NOT built as separate dist files
- packages/theme/src/line.css — Full bundle entry showing all layers
- docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM-IMPLEMENTATION-GUIDE.md:917-941 — Reference exports spec from design guide (Step 6.3)

Approach:
1. DECISION NEEDED: The design guide (Step 6.3) expects subdirectory dist output (dist/colors/amber.min.css, dist/themes/blue.min.css) for wildcard exports (./colors/* -> ./dist/colors/*.min.css). The current build uses flat naming (colors-amber.min.css). Two options:
   A) Update build.ts computeOutFile() to output into subdirectories (colors/, schemas/, themes/, tokens/) and update exports to use wildcard patterns — matches design guide
   B) Keep flat naming and use explicit per-palette exports (./colors/amber -> ./dist/colors-amber.min.css) — more verbose but no build changes needed
   Option A is recommended as it matches the design guide contract.

2. Add individual token family builds: The build script currently excludes tokens/ subdirectory files (they are only consumed via @import by the barrel). Add tokens/*.css to the dirPatterns array so each family (typography, sizing, borders, etc.) gets its own dist output. The bead notes explicitly require this (e.g., @websublime/line-theme/tokens/typography).

3. Add exports for normalize and utilities: Currently built as utils-normalize.min.css and utils-utilities.min.css. If going with subdirectory approach, rename to normalize.min.css and utilities.min.css at the root dist level, or put under utils/ subdir.

4. Final exports map (Option A with subdirs):
   . -> ./dist/line.min.css
   ./reset -> ./dist/reset.min.css
   ./tokens -> ./dist/tokens.min.css
   ./tokens/* -> ./dist/tokens/*.min.css (17 families)
   ./semantic-defaults -> ./dist/semantic-defaults.min.css
   ./aliases -> ./dist/aliases.min.css
   ./normalize -> ./dist/normalize.min.css
   ./utilities -> ./dist/utilities.min.css
   ./colors/* -> ./dist/colors/*.min.css (28 palettes)
   ./schemas/* -> ./dist/schemas/*.min.css (28 schemas)
   ./themes/* -> ./dist/themes/*.min.css (28 themes)

5. Update the files field in package.json if needed (currently dist/ which covers all).

Risks:
- Changing dist output structure from flat to subdirectories is a BREAKING CHANGE for any consumer currently referencing dist files by their flat names. Check if any other package in the monorepo imports from dist paths directly.
- Wildcard exports (./colors/*) require Node 16+ (subpath patterns). Should be fine for modern consumers.
- The custom/ directory (28 custom-*.min.css files) is NOT mentioned in acceptance criteria. Decide whether to expose it via exports or keep it internal.
- utils-media.min.css is 0 bytes in dist — media.css may only contain @custom-media definitions that get stripped by cssnano. Decide whether to export it.

Related tests: No automated tests found for package.json exports resolution. The acceptance criteria says 'Verified by manual import test.'

title: P0-E1-T9: Review and update theme index.html showcase
description:
The theme package has an index.html that serves as a visual test page for the CSS framework. After the branding refactor, it needs a comprehensive review to ensure it showcases ALL CSS features the framework supports: all 28 color palettes (12-level scales), all semantic schema classes, all utility classes (.line-is-*), all CSS custom properties (--line-*), media queries (light/dark), normalize rules, and any other rules/vars defined in the framework. Currently it only shows color scales and a subset of token classes — it should be expanded to be a complete visual reference.

LAYOUT & BRANDING:

The showcase page should be redesigned as an appealing, polished landing-page experience — inspired by Radix Themes / Radix UI documentation pages. Think: clean hero section, well-organized sections with clear headings, smooth scroll, visual hierarchy, generous whitespace, and a professional developer-tool aesthetic. NOT a raw test harness — a showcase that sells the design system.

Use branding assets from the root /branding/ directory:
- branding/logo-wordmark.svg (light mode)
- branding/logo-wordmark-dark.svg (dark mode)
- branding/symbol-mark.svg (light mode)
- branding/symbol-mark-dark.svg (dark mode)

The hero section should prominently feature the line://ui logo and wordmark, with a tagline and smooth entry into the feature sections below.

INTERACTIVE/VISUAL TESTING REQUIREMENTS:

1. Interactive States: Demonstrate hover, focus, active, and focus-visible states on interactive elements. The framework already provides 150ms ease-in-out transitions on .line-is-{palette} (hover bg), .line-is-{palette}-border (hover border/outline), and .line-is-{palette}-ui-background (hover bg). These should be visually exercisable — buttons, cards, and form elements that respond to mouse/keyboard interaction.

2. Click Interactions: Add clickable elements that demonstrate state changes — e.g., toggling active backgrounds, selecting elements, showing how .line-is-active-background and .line-is-ui-active-background respond. Include the .ripple class demo with click-triggered background transitions.

3. Loading States / Spinners: Create CSS-only loading spinner/animation demos using the framework color tokens and transitions. Show spinners in multiple palette colors. Since no @keyframes currently exist in the framework, the showcase should define showcase-local keyframe animations (in style.css, not line.css) to demonstrate how palette tokens can be used for loading indicators.

4. Multiple Themes Simultaneously: Display side-by-side panels/cards each with a different .line-schema-{palette} class applied, proving that multiple schemas can coexist on the same page. Show at least 4-6 different schema panels simultaneously so the user can compare palettes visually.

5. Cross-Palette Color Combinations: Demonstrate mixing palette utility classes — e.g., a .line-is-blue-background container with .line-is-red-border and .line-is-green text children. Show how different palette classes compose together for multi-color UI elements.

6. Dark/Light Mode Toggle: The toggle already works in main.ts (switches html class between dark/light). Enhance with visual feedback — icon swap (sun/moon), label text, or visual indicator showing current mode. Consider adding a CSS transition on the body/html for smooth theme switching.

7. CSS Transitions/Animations Inventory: Showcase all existing transitions in the framework:
   - .line-is-{palette}: all ease-in-out 150ms (hover)
   - .line-is-{palette}-ui-background: colors ease-in-out 150ms (hover)
   - .line-is-{palette}-border: colors ease-in-out 150ms (hover)
   - .ripple: background 0.8s
   - :focus-visible: outline-offset 145ms
   - ::selection styling with transitions
   Each should have a dedicated demo element the user can interact with.

8. Extended Per-Palette Utility Classes: Demo ALL of them per palette: .line-is-{palette}-color, -low-contrast, -high-contrast, -background, -subtle-background, -ui-background, -ui-hover-background, -ui-active-background, -subtle-element-background, -ui-element-background, -solid-background, -hover-solid-background, -low-contrast-background, -high-contrast-background, -border.

9. Miscellaneous Utilities: Demo .carousel scroll-snap classes, .shadown-current-color, .tabular-numbers, .line-is-tiny.

10. Typography Tokens: Font families (sans/serif/mono), weights (1-9), line-heights (0-9), letter-spacing (0-9), font sizes (0-9 + fluid 0-3).

11. Spacing & Size Tokens: --line-size-000 to 15, fluid sizes 1-10, content/header/breakpoint/relative sizes.

12. Shadow Tokens: Shadows 1-6, inner shadows 0-4, dark mode overrides.

- .line-is-{palette}-ui-element-background: bg (7 / 6)
- .line-is-{palette}-solid-background: bg (9 / 4)
- .line-is-{palette}-hover-solid-background: bg (10 / 3)
- .line-is-{palette}-low-contrast-background: bg (11 / 2)
- .line-is-{palette}-high-contrast-background: bg (12 / 1)
- .line-is-{palette}-border: outline+border color (7 / 6), hover (8 / 5), 150ms transition

=== UTILITY/GENERAL CLASSES (packages/theme/src/utils/general.css) ===
Semantic utilities: .line-is-background, .line-is-subtle-background, .line-is-ui-background (with transition), .line-is-hover-background, .line-is-active-background, .line-is-subtle-border (with transition), .line-is-ui-border (with transition), .line-is-ui-hover, .line-is-solid-background (with transition), .line-is-hover-solid, .line-is-low-contrast, .line-is-high-contrast, .line-is-light, .line-is-dark, .line-is-white, .line-is-black
Other utilities: .carousel/.carousel-container/.carousel-slides (scroll-snap), .line-is-tiny (small size), .ripple (background transition 0.8s), .shadown-current-color (box-shadow with currentColor), .tabular-numbers (font-variant-numeric)
Selection styling: ::selection and ::-moz-selection with schema colors

=== CSS CUSTOM PROPERTIES CATEGORIES ===
1. Semantic color tokens (--line-background, --line-subtle-background, --line-ui-background, --line-ui-hover-background, --line-ui-active-background, --line-subtle-border, --line-ui-border, --line-ui-border-hover, --line-solid-background, --line-solid-hover, --line-low-contrast, --line-high-contrast, --line-white, --line-black, --line-light, --line-dark)
2. Palette color tokens (--line-{palette}-1 through --line-{palette}-12 for each of 28 palettes = 336 vars)
3. Font tokens (--font-sans, --font-serif, --font-mono, --font-weight-1..9, --font-lineheight-0..9, --font-letterspacing-0..9, --font-size-0..9, --font-size-fluid-0..3)
4. Size tokens (--size-000, --size-00, --size-1..15, --size-fluid-1..10, --size-content-1..3, --size-header-1..3, --size-xxs/xs/sm/md/lg/xl/xxl, --size-relative-000..15)
5. Shadow tokens (--shadow-color, --shadow-strength, --shadow-1..6, --inner-shadow-highlight, --inner-shadow-0..4)
6. Open Props JIT tokens (--radius-2, --radius-3, --border-size-1..3, --ease-2, --surface-4 — referenced but injected at build time; NOTE: postcss-jit-props is NOT yet activated per TODO in postcss.config.mjs)

=== MEDIA QUERIES (packages/theme/src/utils/media.css) ===
Motion: --motionOK, --motionNotOK
Opacity: --opacityOK, --opacityNotOK
Data: --useDataOK, --useDataNotOK
Color scheme: --OSdark, --OSlight
Contrast: --highContrast, --lowContrast
Orientation: --portrait, --landscape
Display: --HDcolor
Input device: --touch, --stylus, --pointer, --mouse
Breakpoints: --xxs-only/n-above/n-below/phone, --xs-*, --sm-*, --md-*, --lg-*, --xl-*, --xxl-*

=== NORMALIZE RULES (packages/theme/src/utils/normalize.css) ===
Box sizing, margin reset, border/background reset, html block-size/font/scroll-behavior, focus-visible transitions, body min-block-size, heading styles (h1-h6 with font sizes/weights), link styles, media elements, form elements (inputs/buttons/textarea/select), placeholder styling, code/kbd/pre, mark, lists, paragraphs, details/summary, fieldset, dialog (with backdrop blur), menu, tables (with border-radius), hr, figure/figcaption, blockquote/cite, sup

=== TRANSITIONS/ANIMATIONS AVAILABLE ===
- .line-is-{palette}: all ease-in-out 150ms (hover bg change)
- .line-is-{palette}-ui-background: colors ease-in-out 150ms (hover bg change)
- .line-is-{palette}-border: colors ease-in-out 150ms (hover border/outline change)
- .line-is-ui-background: colors ease-in-out delay-150 (general semantic)
- .line-is-ui-border: colors ease-in-out delay-150 (general semantic)
- .line-is-solid-background: colors ease-in-out delay-150 (general semantic)
- .ripple: background 0.8s
- ::selection: all ease-in-out delay-150
- :focus-visible: outline-offset 145ms var(--ease-2), 0.25s on non-active
- No @keyframes animations currently defined

=== DARK/LIGHT MODE MECHANISM ===
- html.dark / html.light classes toggle color-scheme
- @media (prefers-color-scheme: light/dark) sets root --line-* semantic vars
- :where(html):is(.dark) on each palette overrides color scale values
- :is(.dark) :where(.line-schema-*) reverses semantic mapping
- :is(.dark) :where(.line-is-*) adjusts utility class colors

=== FILE LAYERS ===
1. colors/{palette}.css — raw 12-level HSL scales per palette
2. schemas/{palette}.css — semantic mapping + utility classes per palette
3. themes/{palette}-theme.css — bundles: imports colors + schemas
4. custom/{palette}-custom.css — ui-scale-{palette} demo classes for index.html
5. utils/rules.css — base tokens (font, size, shadow, dark shadow override)
6. utils/normalize.css — CSS reset/normalize
7. utils/general.css — semantic utility classes + misc utilities
8. utils/media.css — custom media queries
9. utils/mixins.css — PostCSS mixins (font-size, font-weight)
10. line.css — main bundle (imports utils + themes + custom)
11. style.css — dev page styles (imports all + page-specific UI styles)

Approach:
1. Keep existing index.html structure — extend, do not rewrite
2. Add sections: Typography, Spacing/Sizes, Shadows, Normalize elements, Media queries, Extended per-palette utilities, Multiple themes side-by-side, Cross-palette combos, Interactive states
3. Extend main.ts: add dark/light toggle visual feedback (icon swap), add any new interactive section handlers (e.g., loading spinner toggle, ripple demo clicks)
4. Title should be updated from "Vite + TS" to "line://ui Theme Showcase"
5. Nav title should be updated from "sublime://vitamin" to "line://ui"

Risks:
- Open Props JIT tokens (--radius-*, --border-size-*, --ease-*, --surface-*) are referenced in normalize.css but postcss-jit-props is NOT activated (TODO in postcss.config.mjs). These will be undefined at runtime. Supervisor must either activate the plugin or define fallback values.
- style.css and line.css have identical import structures — style.css is for dev (index.html), line.css is the production bundle. Changes should target style.css for showcase, not line.css.
- Some general.css transitions use "delay-150" (invalid — should be "150ms"). Might be a bug or a PostCSS simple-vars reference.

Related tests: No test files found for theme package.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: All CSS classes in packages/theme use unprefixed naming (.schema-*, .is-*) that must be migrated to .line-schema-*, .line-is-* per PRD 9.14.

FILES (requiring changes):
- packages/theme/src/schemas/*.css (28 files) -- each contains 2 .schema-{palette} selectors and ~34 .is-{palette}-* selectors (56 + 952 = 1008 occurrences)
- packages/theme/src/utils/general.css:13-100 -- 17 generic .is-* utility classes (is-background, is-subtle-background, is-ui-background, etc.)
- packages/theme/index.html:9-643 -- demo HTML uses schema-* as CSS classes (body class, data-theme attributes, and .is-* utility classes throughout)
- packages/theme/src/main.ts:15-16 -- reads data-theme attribute values (schema-*) and sets them as body class; must be updated to line-schema-*

NOT affected:
- packages/core/ -- zero references to .schema-* or .is-* classes
- packages/theme/src/themes/ -- zero references (only palette CSS vars)
- packages/theme/src/style.css -- no .schema-* or .is-* references (only CSS var refs)

UNIQUE CLASS NAMES:
.schema-* classes: 28 palettes (amber, blue, bronze, brown, crimson, cyan, gold, grass, gray, green, indigo, lime, mauve, mint, olive, orange, pink, plum, purple, red, sage, sand, sky, slate, teal, tomato, violet, yellow)
.is-* generic (utils/general.css): 17 classes (is-background, is-subtle-background, is-ui-background, is-hover-background, is-active-background, is-subtle-border, is-ui-border, is-ui-hover, is-solid-background, is-hover-solid, is-low-contrast, is-high-contrast, is-light, is-dark, is-white, is-black, is-tiny)
.is-{palette} base: 28 (one per palette)
.is-{palette}-{suffix}: 15 suffix variants x 28 palettes = 420 unique class names (color, low-contrast, high-contrast, background, subtle-background, ui-background, ui-hover-background, ui-active-background, subtle-element-background, ui-element-background, solid-background, hover-solid-background, low-contrast-background, high-contrast-background, border)

TOTAL OCCURRENCES: ~1025 in CSS files + ~85 in index.html

EDGE CASES:
1. :is() pseudo-class -- 504 uses of :is(.dark) and :is(:dark) in schema files as parent selectors for dark mode. These are CSS :is() pseudo-class calls, NOT .is-* class names. They must NOT be renamed. The .dark class inside :is(.dark) is also NOT an .is-* class -- it is a .dark class.
2. :where() wrapper -- All .schema-* and .is-* selectors are wrapped in :where() for zero specificity. The rename is a simple string replacement inside :where().
3. Nested selectors -- .is-{palette}-ui-background contains &:hover nested rules. Rename only the class name, not the nesting.
4. data-theme attributes in index.html contain schema-* values (28 buttons). These are string values, not CSS selectors.
5. main.ts line 16: bodyElement.classList.value is set from dataset.theme -- the data-theme values in HTML drive this, so both HTML and conceptually the JS flow must be consistent.

APPROACH:
1. Rename in CSS schemas (28 files): sed .schema-{name} -> .line-schema-{name} and .is-{name} -> .line-is-{name} in all schema CSS files. CAREFUL: do NOT touch :is( pseudo-class -- only replace dot-prefixed class names.
2. Rename in utils/general.css: .is-{utility} -> .line-is-{utility} for all 17 classes.
3. Update index.html: rename class='schema-*' to class='line-schema-*', data-theme='schema-*' to data-theme='line-schema-*', and all is-* class usages to line-is-*.
4. Update index.html body class: schema-gray -> line-schema-gray.
5. Run build to verify no broken references.
6. Grep entire repo for any remaining .schema-* or bare .is-* (excluding :is pseudo-class) to confirm zero legacy names.

RISKS:
- Regex must distinguish .is-{name} (class selector to rename) from :is( (CSS pseudo-class, do NOT rename). Safe pattern: replace literal dot-prefixed '.is-' but never ':is('.
- The .dark and .light classes used inside :is(.dark) and :is(:dark) are NOT in scope for this task.
- Some schema files use :is(:dark) with a colon (pseudo-class syntax) while others use :is(.dark) with a dot (class selector). Neither should be modified by this task.

RELATED TESTS: No test files found for the theme package. Validation is build-based (acceptance criteria says build succeeds).

SIBLING TASKS: This task is independent of T2 (palette CSS vars) and T3 (semantic CSS vars) but all must complete before T8 (validate branding refactor).

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: 16 unprefixed semantic CSS variables are declared in schema files, rules.css, and referenced in general.css and style.css. These need --line-* prefix per PRD 9.14.

SEMANTIC VARIABLES TO RENAME (16 total):
  --background -> --line-background
  --subtle-background -> --line-subtle-background
  --ui-background -> --line-ui-background
  --ui-hover-background -> --line-ui-hover-background
  --ui-active-background -> --line-ui-active-background
  --subtle-border -> --line-subtle-border
  --ui-border -> --line-ui-border
  --ui-border-hover -> --line-ui-border-hover
  --solid-background -> --line-solid-background
  --solid-hover -> --line-solid-hover
  --low-contrast -> --line-low-contrast
  --high-contrast -> --line-high-contrast
  --light -> --line-light
  --dark -> --line-dark
  --white -> --line-white
  --black -> --line-black

FILES WITH DECLARATIONS (LHS):
  - packages/theme/src/schemas/*.css (28 files, 760 occurrences) — each schema declares 12 core semantic vars + --light/--dark in light block, some also in dark block. 15 schemas also declare --white/--black.
  - packages/theme/src/utils/rules.css (28 occurrences) — declares semantic vars with HSL values for light/dark media queries, plus --white/--black.

FILES WITH REFERENCES (var()):
  - packages/theme/src/utils/general.css (23 occurrences) — utility classes referencing semantic vars.
  - packages/theme/src/style.css (14 occurrences) — body styles and demo UI classes referencing semantic vars.

TOTAL OCCURRENCES: ~825 across 31 files.

DO NOT RENAME (out of scope):
  - Open Props utility tokens: --font-*, --size-*, --radius-*, --border-size-*, --shadow-*, --ease-* (declared in rules.css, referenced in normalize.css). These are handled by postcss-jit-props in a separate task (line-ui-c5q.1).
  - --shadow-color, --shadow-strength, --inner-shadow-highlight (part of shadow system in rules.css).
  - --nice-inner-radius (local scoped variable in normalize.css table styles).
  - --surface-4 (referenced in normalize.css:242 fieldset border — appears to be a stale/undefined reference, not a semantic variable).

EDGE CASES:
  1. Amber schema has --light/--dark in BOTH light and dark blocks (4 occurrences). All other schemas have them only in the light block (2 occurrences). This is an existing inconsistency — rename as-is, do not fix.
  2. 15 of 28 schemas have --white/--black. The other 13 do not. This is existing inconsistency — rename what exists.
  3. --light and --dark are short names that could false-match (e.g., .dark, :is(.dark), color-scheme: dark). Use word-boundary-aware replacement. The CSS variable form --light/--dark should match, but NOT .dark or color-scheme: dark.
  4. style.css contains demo/playground UI styles that reference semantic variables. These must also be updated.

NO REFERENCES IN packages/core/ — zero semantic variable references in core package CSS, TS, or JS files.
NO REFERENCES IN packages/theme/src/custom/ — custom files do not use semantic variables.
NO REFERENCES IN packages/theme/src/themes/ — theme files are just imports.

Approach:
  1. Create branch feature/p0-e1-t3-prefix-semantic-variables from next (or from the t2 branch if merging serially).
  2. For each of the 16 semantic variable names, do a find-and-replace across packages/theme/src/schemas/, packages/theme/src/utils/rules.css, packages/theme/src/utils/general.css, and packages/theme/src/style.css.
  3. The replacement is straightforward: --{name} -> --line-{name} wherever it appears as a CSS custom property (both declarations and var() references).
  4. Use sed or similar: replace occurrences of '--background' with '--line-background' etc., being careful of word boundaries (e.g., --subtle-background should not also match --background; process longer names first).
  5. Run build: cd packages/theme && bun run build.
  6. Verify: grep for any remaining unprefixed semantic variables.

Risks:
  - False positives on short variable names (--light, --dark, --white, --black). These could match substrings. Use precise regex with word boundaries.
  - Ordering of replacements matters: replace --subtle-background before --background, --ui-border-hover before --ui-border, etc. (longest-first).
  - --surface-4 in normalize.css:242 is a stale reference (undefined variable). Not part of this task but worth noting — it will remain broken.

Related tests: No CSS-specific test files found in packages/theme. Build validation (bun run build) is the primary verification.

title: Reset _imageError state when imageSrc property changes in sc-product-card
description:
File: sc-product-card.ts:223-225

The `_imageError` reactive state is set to `true` when the image `onerror` event fires, causing the placeholder to render. However, this state is never reset when the `imageSrc` property is updated by the consumer.

Consequence: if a consumer updates `imageSrc` after an error (e.g. retrying with a corrected URL), the component continues rendering the error placeholder instead of attempting to load the new image.

Recommended fix: clear `_imageError = false` inside the `imageSrc` property setter (or in `updated()` when `imageSrc` is in the changed map) so that a new source always triggers a fresh load attempt.

title: Note ::part() + pseudo-class browser support limitation in pattern guide
description:
File: playground.ts:284

The pattern `sc-product-card::part(button):hover` works correctly in modern browsers. However, the combination of `::part()` with pseudo-classes (`:hover`, `:focus`, `:active`) has limited support in older rendering engines — specifically Chromium < 73, Firefox < 72, and no support in IE/legacy Edge.

Since the showcase targets modern browsers, this usage is acceptable today. The finding is a prompt to document this limitation in the pattern guide so consumers of line://ui are aware before adopting the same pattern in products that must support older browsers.

title: Document JSON attribute requirement for colors Array property in sc-product-card
description:
File: sc-product-card.ts:49

The `colors` property is declared with `type: Array` in the `@property` decorator. Lit's default Array converter uses `JSON.parse` for attribute-based binding, so passing the value as an HTML attribute (e.g. `colors='["red","blue"]'`) requires valid JSON syntax.

Current usage relies exclusively on dot-binding (`.colors=${...}`), which bypasses the converter and works correctly. However, any future consumer who attempts attribute-based usage will be silently broken without a clear error message.

Recommended fix: add a JSDoc note to the property explaining that attribute-based usage requires a valid JSON array string, and that dot-binding is the preferred pattern.

title: Narrow transition properties on .chip to avoid layout thrashing via ::part()
description:
File: sc-product-card.ts:187

`transition: all 150ms ease-in-out` on the .chip element is overly broad. When consumers set dimensional properties (width, height, padding) via `::part(chip)`, the catch-all transition will animate those as well, causing unexpected layout thrashing.

Recommended fix: replace `all` with an explicit list of animated properties — `background, color, border-color` — or whatever the component intentionally transitions.

title: Undocumented hover state on cart button uses --line-solid-hover (not in spec token table)
description:
## Finding

The cart button in the E-commerce product card block applies `--line-solid-hover` on `:hover`. This token is not listed in the spec token table for the component (line-ui-m3d.3) and was added as a UX improvement beyond the specified surface.

## Context

The addition is sensible — hover feedback on an interactive button is expected behaviour and aligns with the theme system's intent for `--line-solid-hover`. However, no spec update was logged to record this intentional extension.

## Impact

Low. The token is a valid part of the design system and the visual result is correct. The gap is purely documentary: the spec does not reflect the actual implementation.

## Resolution

Either:
- Update the spec token table for the product card block to include `--line-solid-hover` as an accepted interactive state token on the cart button.
- Or add a brief design note to line-ui-m3d.3 acknowledging the addition so reviewers know it was deliberate.

No code change is required.

title: Add ::part attributes to inner product card elements
description: Code review finding from line-ui-m3d.3: Only the product-card wrapper divs have part attributes (product-card-1, product-card-2). Consider adding ::part() to inner elements (price, rating, cart button) to enable consumer styling of individual card sections. File: apps/showcase/src/pages/playground.ts:521,555. Severity: suggestion.

title: Guard _resolveAllSizes probe against stale computed values if theme CSS loads after firstUpdated
description:
File: apps/showcase/src/pages/typography.ts:192-209

The `_resolveAllSizes` helper appends a temporary element to `document.body` and reads `getComputedStyle` synchronously inside `firstUpdated`. If the theme CSS has not fully parsed by the time `firstUpdated` fires, the returned computed values will be the fallback (unresolved) values rather than the actual token values, silently producing stale size data.

Risk is currently low because:
1. The showcase loads its theme CSS synchronously in the HTML `<head>`.
2. The same pattern is used without issue in `spacing.ts`.

However, this is a latent race condition. If the loading strategy ever changes (e.g., dynamic import, lazy stylesheet, CI environment with slower CSS parsing), the probe could silently read wrong values without any error.

Suggested mitigation: defer the probe to `requestAnimationFrame` or listen for a `load` / `CSSStyleSheet.replace` completion signal before reading computed styles. Alternatively, add an explicit guard that checks whether the resolved value is the expected non-fallback unit before trusting it.

title: Fix incorrect token name --line-lineheight-3 used across showcase (should be --line-font-lineheight-3)
description:
File: apps/showcase/src/pages/typography.ts:231 (and recurs throughout the showcase app)

The token reference `--line-lineheight-3` is incorrect. The correct token name is `--line-font-lineheight-3`. Because the property falls back to `1.6` the showcase renders fine visually, but the token reference is silently broken and will not reflect any future token value changes.

This is a pre-existing issue not introduced by PR line-ui-6zy.5. The same incorrect name appears in at least the following files:
- apps/showcase/src/pages/spacing.ts
- apps/showcase/src/pages/colors.ts
- apps/showcase/src/pages/surfaces.ts
- apps/showcase/src/pages/home.ts
- apps/showcase/src/pages/motion.ts
- apps/showcase/src/components/sc-section.ts
- apps/showcase/src/components/sc-code-block.ts

The fix requires a global search-and-replace of `--line-lineheight-` → `--line-font-lineheight-` across the entire showcase app, followed by a visual smoke-test to confirm no regressions.

title: Fix stale comment: Font Families section header says '(19)' but should say '(18)'
description:
File: apps/showcase/src/pages/typography.ts:439

The comment heading for the Font Families section reads "Font Families (19)" but the actual array contains 18 entries. This is a documentation-only inaccuracy — the count in the comment does not match the array length or the documented deviation in the spec.

The fix is a one-line comment update: change '(19)' to '(18)' to accurately reflect the number of visualised font-family tokens.

title: Reduce gradient duplication in :host([light]) .comp-image-placeholder with a CSS custom property
description: apps/showcase/src/pages/home.ts:431-449 — The :host([light]) override for .comp-image-placeholder duplicates the full gradient declaration from the default block, with only the mix-intensity percentage differing between the two. This creates a maintenance burden: any change to the gradient structure must be applied in both places in sync. Fix: introduce a CSS custom property (e.g., --_image-placeholder-mix-intensity) with a default value in the base rule, and override only that property inside :host([light]). This eliminates the structural duplication while keeping the visual difference explicit.

title: Replace hardcoded font-weight: 800 with design token var(--line-font-weight-8) in home.ts
description: apps/showcase/src/pages/home.ts:224,495 — The value font-weight: 800 is hardcoded at two locations in the static styles block. The file otherwise consistently uses design tokens via CSS custom properties (e.g., var(--line-*)). Hardcoding this value breaks the token convention and means a future change to the font weight scale would require a manual find-and-replace in source files rather than a single token update. Fix: replace both occurrences with var(--line-font-weight-8), consistent with the --line-* naming convention used across the design system.

title: Type NavCard.key as PanelKey instead of string in home.ts
description: apps/showcase/src/pages/home.ts:10-16 — The NavCard interface declares the key property as type string. The app.ts file already exports a PanelKey union type that represents all valid panel route keys. By using string here instead of importing and applying PanelKey, the compile-time guarantee that NavCard entries always reference valid panels is lost. A typo or stale key would only surface at runtime. Fix: import PanelKey from app.ts and annotate NavCard.key as PanelKey. This is a low-effort change with meaningful safety benefit.

title: Show computed px equivalent alongside rem values in spacing page rem section
description:
File: apps/showcase/src/pages/spacing.ts (rem sizes section)

The spec (SHOWCASE-APP-SPEC) states that visual bars should display both rem and px values. The current implementation only shows the rem value. During the investigation phase a `px` field was proposed for the REM_SIZES data structure but was not carried through to the final implementation.

Adding the computed px equivalent (e.g., 1rem = 16px at default root font-size) alongside the rem label would improve the educational value of the spacing page and align with the spec intent.

Source: code review of line-ui-6zy.6 (Spacing page implementation).

title: Add explanatory comment to hardcoded font-size: 9px in spacing page
description:
File: apps/showcase/src/pages/spacing.ts, line 397

A hardcoded `font-size: 9px` is used without any explanatory comment. The motion page documents this same pattern with an inline comment at line 506 explaining the intent. For consistency and maintainability, the same comment should be added to the spacing page.

Source: code review of line-ui-6zy.6 (Spacing page implementation).

title: Add implementation guidance for withThemeByClassName setting both class and colorScheme
description:
File: .spec/STORYBOOK-SPEC.md:449

The withThemeByClassName decorator note states it 'should also set style.colorScheme' but provides no implementation guidance on how to do so.

This is acceptable at the spec level, but the Storybook implementation task (line-ui-gvz.1 — Setup Storybook 8) must address the concrete mechanism: the decorator needs to set both the className on the story root element and the style.colorScheme property so that native browser APIs (e.g., scrollbar theming, form control colours) align with the active palette. Without explicit guidance, implementors may only wire up the class toggle and omit the colorScheme property, causing a partial dark-mode integration.
close_reason: QA passed. All acceptance criteria met. Companion decorator guidance added to STORYBOOK-SPEC.md with correct execution order explanation. No deviations.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The STORYBOOK-SPEC.md code sample for the mode decorator (lines 272-279) uses withThemeByClassName which only toggles CSS classes. The prose at lines 287 and 289 says it 'should also set style.colorScheme' but provides no implementation guidance. The withThemeByClassName API from @storybook/addon-themes has no built-in mechanism for setting inline styles — it only adds/removes classes. Implementors following the code sample will get class toggles but miss the colorScheme property, causing light-dark() tokens to not respond to mode changes.

Files:
- .spec/STORYBOOK-SPEC.md:272-279 — Mode decorator code sample (only sets class, no colorScheme)
- .spec/STORYBOOK-SPEC.md:287 — Prose says 'should also set style.colorScheme' but no HOW
- .spec/STORYBOOK-SPEC.md:289 — Repeats the requirement without implementation detail
- .spec/STORYBOOK-SPEC.md:447 — Section 7.1 repeats 'should also set style.colorScheme' without guidance
- .spec/STORYBOOK-SPEC.md:624 — Section on programmatic toggle shows the pattern: document.documentElement.style.colorScheme = 'dark'
- .spec/SHOWCASE-APP-SPEC.md:400-401 — Reference pattern: primary trigger is style.colorScheme, secondary is .dark/.light class

Approach:
1. Add a custom wrapper decorator or a companion decorator after the withThemeByClassName mode decorator in the preview.ts code sample (lines 272-283). Three options exist:
   Option A (recommended): Add a custom Storybook decorator that observes the html element class and sets style.colorScheme accordingly. Place it after the withThemeByClassName decorators in the array so it runs in the correct order.
   Option B: Replace the mode withThemeByClassName with a fully custom decorator that sets both the class AND style.colorScheme in one pass.
   Option C: Use a MutationObserver in preview.ts that watches html class changes and syncs colorScheme.
2. Update the code sample in section 4.2 (preview.ts) to include the chosen mechanism with inline comments explaining why both class and colorScheme are needed.
3. Update the prose at lines 287 and 289 to reference the code sample rather than leaving 'should also set' as a vague instruction.
4. Update section 7.1 (line 447) similarly — replace 'should also set' with a cross-reference to the implementation in section 4.2.

Risks:
- withThemeByClassName applies classes asynchronously via Storybook's decorator lifecycle — a companion decorator must account for execution order
- The Light theme maps to empty string ('') for class (line 274), meaning no class is added; the companion decorator must handle both the 'add dark class' and 'remove dark class' cases
- Storybook iframe isolation: document.documentElement in the preview iframe is NOT the same as the parent Storybook shell — the decorator runs in the correct iframe context, but this should be noted

description:

title: Dark-mode bloom @keyframes variants for motion page
description: The motion page (apps/showcase/src/pages/motion.ts) includes all 23 @keyframes in static styles for shadow DOM isolation, but only the light-mode bloom variants (brightness(2)). The dark-mode variants from animations.css use brightness(0.5). Wiring these requires integrating with the showcase's :host([light]) theme-switching mechanism — not a safe refactoring change. Discovered during review of line-ui-6zy.7.
close_reason: QA passed. All tests, build, lint green. Implementation approved and validated.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The motion page (apps/showcase/src/pages/motion.ts) defines all 23 @keyframes in its static styles for shadow DOM isolation. The two bloom keyframes (fade-in-bloom, fade-out-bloom) use brightness(2) at the 10% mark — the light-mode variant. The source animations.css has dark-mode variants inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) that use brightness(0.5) instead. The motion page has no dark-mode variants at all.

Key challenge: The showcase app does NOT use prefers-color-scheme for theme switching. It uses a manual toggle that sets html.light/html.dark classes and color-scheme property on the document root. Inside shadow DOM, @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) would only respond to OS preference, not the showcase toggle. Currently no page component receives a light property from the app — only sc-nav does.

Files:
- apps/showcase/src/pages/motion.ts:666-670 — fade-in-bloom @keyframes (light-mode only, brightness(2))
- apps/showcase/src/pages/motion.ts:677-681 — fade-out-bloom @keyframes (light-mode only, brightness(2))
- packages/theme/src/tokens/animations.css:260-292 — dark-mode bloom variants (brightness(0.5)) inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)
- apps/showcase/src/app.ts:113-121 — _applyMode() sets html.light/html.dark classes + color-scheme
- apps/showcase/src/app.ts:174-199 — _renderPanel() does NOT pass light prop to any page
- apps/showcase/src/styles/showcase.css:8-13 — html color-scheme: dark (default) and html.light color-scheme: light

Approach:
1. Add a light boolean property (reflected attribute) to sc-page-motion, same pattern as sc-nav
2. In app.ts _renderPanel(), pass ?light=${this._light} to <sc-page-motion>
3. In motion.ts static styles, keep the current bloom @keyframes as default (light-mode: brightness(2))
4. Add :host(:not([light])) scoped dark-mode bloom @keyframes that use brightness(0.5) — NOTE: @keyframes cannot be scoped inside :host() selectors in CSS. Two alternatives:
   Option A (recommended): Use CSS custom properties for the bloom brightness value. Define --_bloom-brightness: 0.5 on :host (dark default) and --_bloom-brightness: 2 on :host([light]). Then the @keyframes reference filter: brightness(var(--_bloom-brightness)). This is clean and CSS-only.
   Option B: Define two sets of @keyframes (fade-in-bloom-light/fade-in-bloom-dark etc.) and dynamically pick the right keyframe name in the render method based on the light property. More complex, more code.

Risks:
- @keyframes do NOT support var() in all browsers for filter values — need to verify. If unsupported, Option B (separate keyframe names) becomes necessary.
- Adding light prop to motion page sets a precedent — other pages may need the same pattern later. Consider whether a mixin or shared approach is warranted (likely overkill for now, just one page).
- The existing bloom keyframes in motion.ts have brightness(2) which matches the light-mode source in animations.css. Dark mode (the showcase default) should use brightness(0.5), so the current default is actually wrong for the default dark mode.

Related tests: No test files found for the motion page specifically. This is a showcase/demo page, not a library component.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text: DECISION: Used CSS custom property (Option A from investigation) instead of duplicate keyframes (Option B) because var() inside @keyframes for filter is well-supported in all modern browsers (Chrome 49+, Firefox 31+, Safari 15.4+) and keeps code minimal.

title: Add intermediate font-size tokens between --line-font-size-0 and --line-font-size-1
description:
Hardcoded px font-sizes (9px, 10px, 11px) appear in sc-swatch.ts, sc-code-block.ts, and colors.ts (apps/showcase/). No token equivalents exist between --line-font-size-0 (8px) and --line-font-size-1 (12px), leaving a gap that forces showcase components to use raw px values instead of design tokens.

Consider adding intermediate font-size tokens to the theme package (e.g., --line-font-size-00 at ~10px) so showcase components can reference them consistently.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The font-size token scale jumps from --line-font-size-0 (0.5rem / 8px) to --line-font-size-1 (0.75rem / 12px), leaving no token for 9px, 10px, or 11px. Showcase components and the core inspector use hardcoded px values to fill this gap.

Files:
- packages/theme/src/tokens/typography.css:89-90 — where --line-font-size-0 (0.5rem) and --line-font-size-1 (0.75rem) are defined; new tokens go here
- apps/showcase/src/pages/colors.ts:138,145,204,246,346,421 — hardcoded 9px, 10px, 11px font-sizes
- apps/showcase/src/components/sc-code-block.ts:34,45 — hardcoded 10px and 11px font-sizes
- apps/showcase/src/components/sc-swatch.ts:69,88 — hardcoded 10px and 11px font-sizes
- packages/core/src/lib/ui/inspector.ts:59 — hardcoded 10px font-size (may or may not adopt tokens; inspector is isolated)
- packages/theme/test/token-parity.test.ts:73 — lineOnlyTokens array must be updated with new token names
- packages/theme/src/utils/mixins.css:1-3 — font-size mixin uses $(size) interpolation; new names must work with it

Approach:
1. Choose naming convention. Two viable options:
   a) RECOMMENDED: Use --line-font-size-00 as a single intermediate (10px / 0.625rem). This mirrors how Open Props originally used --font-size-00. Only one new token needed — most hardcoded values are 10px or 11px, and 11px rounds cleanly to --line-font-size-1 (12px). 9px is close enough to --line-font-size-0 (8px) for showcase display purposes.
   b) ALTERNATIVE: Add three tokens using double-zero notation: --line-font-size-00 (9px/0.5625rem), --line-font-size-01 (10px/0.625rem), --line-font-size-02 (11px/0.6875rem). More precise but adds complexity and non-standard naming.
2. Add the chosen token(s) to typography.css between size-0 and size-1
3. Update the header comment token count (currently says '10 static')
4. Update token-parity.test.ts lineOnlyTokens array to include new token name(s)
5. Update snapshot tests (bun test --update in packages/theme)
6. Replace hardcoded px values in showcase components with the new token(s)
7. Optionally replace the inspector.ts 10px (low priority — inspector styles are isolated/internal)

Risks:
- The font-size mixin uses $(size) interpolation. Passing '00' would produce var(--line-font-size-00) which works fine. But '01'/'02' would be unusual.
- Naming --line-font-size-00 for 10px could confuse developers who expect 00 < 0 (like sizing scale where --line-size-00 = -0.25rem). But for font-size the negative semantics don't apply, and OP originally used font-size-00 for its smallest size.
- Snapshot tests will need regeneration.

- packages/theme/test/__snapshots__/snapshot.test.ts.snap — must regenerate

description:

title: Scope noUnknownAtRules: off to CSS files only via Biome override
description:
Finding from code review of line-ui-p3v.5.

File: biome.json, line 50

Currently `noUnknownAtRules` is set to `"off"` globally in the `suspicious` rules section of biome.json. Since all CSS in this project is PostCSS-processed (using at-rules like `@mixin`, `@apply`, `@custom-media`, etc. that are not standard CSS), this suppression is necessary. However, the rule is disabled project-wide rather than scoped to CSS files only.

The suggestion is to move this override into a Biome `overrides` block targeting only CSS/PostCSS files (e.g., `"include": ["**/*.css"]`), so that the rule remains active for non-CSS files (TypeScript, JavaScript) where unknown at-rules would be a genuine lint signal.

Low priority: no correctness issue today since the project has no non-PostCSS CSS, but scoping it properly is cleaner hygiene and future-proofs the config against accidental suppression of real issues in TS/JS files.

title: Refine ambient type declarations for postcss-preset-env and cssnano to eliminate as any casts
description:
Finding from code review of line-ui-p3v.6 (chore/line-ui-p3v-6-postcss-plugin-dedup branch).

File: packages/theme/src/postcss-pipeline.ts, lines 48 and 66.
Supporting file: packages/theme/src/postcss-plugins.d.ts, lines 28-32 and 40-44.

Both postcssPresetEnv and cssNano are called with plugin-specific option shapes but their ambient module declarations in postcss-plugins.d.ts type the options parameter as Record<string, unknown> via PluginCreator<Record<string, unknown>>. Because the concrete option objects ({ autoprefixer, features, stage } for postcss-preset-env and { preset } for cssnano) do not satisfy Record<string, unknown> strictly enough for TypeScript to infer them without widening, both call sites require an as any cast.

The casts are non-blocking and pre-existed before the consolidation in line-ui-p3v.6, where they were moved as-is. The fix is to replace the generic Record<string, unknown> with narrower option interfaces in postcss-plugins.d.ts, giving TypeScript enough information to accept the call sites without casting.

title: Revisit createProcessor() duplication with postcss.config.mjs when config stabilizes
description:
File: packages/theme/src/build.ts, lines 35-81.

The createProcessor() function duplicates the PostCSS plugin chain that is already declared in postcss.config.mjs. Both locations configure the same set of plugins (import, mixins, simple-vars, nested, preset-env, custom-media, cssnano) independently.

During the auto-discovery build refactor (line-ui-c5q.6) this consolidation was explicitly skipped for two reasons:
1. Dynamically importing postcss.config.mjs inside build.ts would alter lazy-loading behaviour and introduce a runtime dependency on the config file format.
2. Coupling the programmatic build path to the config file adds fragility when either side evolves.

The safer interim measure — adding cross-reference comments in both files — was applied instead.

This issue tracks revisiting the consolidation once the PostCSS config has stabilised and the lazy-loading tradeoff can be re-evaluated without risk of breaking the build pipeline.
close_reason: QA passed. All acceptance criteria met. 118/118 CSS entries build correctly. Merging to remote.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: build.ts:35-81 (createProcessor) and postcss.config.mjs:15-43 declare identical PostCSS plugin chains independently. The 7 plugins and all postcssPresetEnv feature flags are byte-for-byte equivalent. Cross-reference comments exist but the configs are fully decoupled.

Files:
- packages/theme/src/build.ts:35-81 — createProcessor() with lazy dynamic imports of 7 PostCSS plugins
- packages/theme/postcss.config.mjs:1-43 — Static ESM config with same 7 plugins and identical options
- packages/theme/package.json:9 — build script uses build.ts; dev script uses Vite (which auto-discovers postcss.config.mjs)

Who uses what:
- postcss.config.mjs is consumed by: (1) Vite dev server (vite dev auto-discovers it), (2) potentially postcss-cli (still in devDependencies but no longer referenced in scripts)
- build.ts createProcessor() is consumed by: bun run src/build.ts (the production build)

Approach — three viable strategies:

OPTION A: Shared factory module (RECOMMENDED)
Create packages/theme/src/postcss-plugins.ts exporting an async function that returns the plugin array. Both build.ts and postcss.config.mjs import from it. postcss.config.mjs becomes a thin wrapper: import { getPlugins } from './src/postcss-plugins.ts'; export default { plugins: await getPlugins() }. This preserves lazy-loading in build.ts (call the factory when needed) and keeps postcss.config.mjs as the Vite-discoverable config.

OPTION B: Dynamic import of postcss.config.mjs in build.ts
Replace createProcessor() body with: const config = await import('../postcss.config.mjs'); return postcss(config.default.plugins). Simpler but couples build.ts to the config file format. The TODO comment in postcss.config.mjs about adding postcss-jit-props (line-ui-c5q.1) means the config WILL change — coupling is acceptable since both must stay in sync anyway.

OPTION C: Leave as-is with stronger enforcement
Keep duplication but add a build-time assertion or test that compares plugin lists. Lowest risk, but does not eliminate the duplication.

Risks:
- postcss.config.mjs has a pending TODO (line-ui-c5q.1) to add postcss-jit-props. Any consolidation must account for this upcoming change.
- Vite auto-discovers postcss.config.mjs by convention. If it becomes a .ts file or moves, Vite will lose its PostCSS config. postcss.config.mjs must remain at the package root.
- postcss-cli is still listed in devDependencies but is no longer used in any script (legacy from pre-build.ts era). It can be removed as a cleanup.
- The lazy-loading pattern in createProcessor() (Promise.all of dynamic imports) is intentional for startup perf. Option A preserves this; Option B loses it (config imports are static ESM).

Related tests: No dedicated test files for the PostCSS pipeline. The build is validated by running 'bun run build' and checking dist/ output.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The bead description says only indigo.css dark block is missing --line-light/--line-dark. However, investigation reveals the scope is MUCH larger: 27 out of 28 schema files are missing these tokens in their dark block. Only amber.css has them. The pattern for dark mode swaps values: --line-light maps to {palette}-12 and --line-dark maps to {palette}-1 (inverted from light mode).

Files:
- packages/theme/src/schemas/indigo.css:19-33 -- dark block missing --line-light and --line-dark (as stated in bead)
- packages/theme/src/schemas/amber.css:32-33 -- ONLY palette with correct dark block (reference implementation)
- All other 26 schema files (blue, bronze, brown, crimson, cyan, gold, grass, gray, green, lime, mauve, mint, olive, orange, pink, plum, purple, red, sage, sand, sky, slate, teal, tomato, violet, yellow) -- all missing --line-light/--line-dark in dark block

Secondary finding (separate inconsistency, out of scope but noted):
- 15 palettes have --line-white/--line-black tokens in light block; 13 palettes do not. Neither group has these in their dark block.
- Palettes WITH --line-white/--line-black: mint, olive, orange, pink, plum, purple, red, sage, sand, sky, slate, teal, tomato, violet, yellow
- Palettes WITHOUT: amber, blue, bronze, brown, crimson, cyan, gold, grass, gray, green, indigo, lime, mauve

Approach:
1. For each of the 27 affected schema files, add two lines after --line-high-contrast in the dark block:
   --line-light: var(--line-{palette}-12); /* Light text */
   --line-dark: var(--line-{palette}-1); /* Dark text */
   These go BEFORE --line-solid-text and AFTER --line-high-contrast, matching amber.css structure.
2. Verify all 28 dark blocks have identical token count after the fix (should be 15 tokens each).
3. Build the theme package to verify no CSS errors.

Risks:
- No tests exist for the theme package, so verification is manual/build-only.
- The --line-white/--line-black inconsistency is a separate issue and should NOT be addressed in this bead to keep scope contained. A new finding bead should be created for it.
- Consumers relying on --line-light/--line-dark in dark mode currently get the light-mode value (inherited, not overridden), which means they get {palette}-1 for --line-light instead of the correct {palette}-12. This is a real bug affecting dark mode text color.

acceptance_criteria: reset.css exists in packages/theme/src/ using only :where() selectors to ensure zero specificity. File is optional — consumers opt in explicitly. Covers common light-DOM and slotted content resets. Referenced in theme package.json exports. Documented with a usage example in the showcase.
close_reason: QA passed. All acceptance criteria met, build/lint/typecheck clean, reset.min.css produced correctly.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: No reset.css file exists yet in packages/theme/src/. ARCHITECTURE.md section 14.10 specifies an optional consumer-side reset using :where() selectors for slotted/light-DOM content. The only example given targets line-field (label, hint slot, error slot). The file must be created from scratch, registered in the build pipeline, and exported from package.json.

Files:
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1023-1038 — Section 14.10 defines the contract: :where() selectors, zero specificity, targets slotted/light-DOM content within line-* custom elements
- packages/theme/src/line.css — Main CSS bundle entry point; reset.css must NOT be imported here (it is optional, consumers opt in explicitly)
- packages/theme/src/build.ts:136-148 — Build entry discovery; reset.css at src/ root level will be auto-discovered and output as reset.min.css (no build.ts changes needed)
- packages/theme/package.json — Needs 'exports' field added with './reset' mapping to './dist/reset.min.css'
- packages/theme/src/utils/normalize.css — Existing document-level normalize (NOT :where()-only); reset.css is a separate concern targeting component slotted content
- packages/theme/src/utils/utilities.css — Example of :where() pattern already used in the project

Approach:
1. Create packages/theme/src/reset.css with :where() selectors covering common slotted/light-DOM content resets. Architecture specifies line-field example; extend to other components that accept slotted content (line-dialog, line-card, line-alert, line-tooltip, line-popover, etc.)
2. All selectors MUST use :where() wrapper for zero specificity — this is the key differentiator from normalize.css
3. Cover common light-DOM elements that appear as slotted content: labels, spans, paragraphs, headings, lists, images, links, buttons, inputs within field wrappers
4. Do NOT add @import of reset.css to line.css — the file must remain opt-in only
5. Add package.json exports entry: './reset' -> './dist/reset.min.css'
6. Build pipeline (build.ts) auto-discovers root-level CSS files in src/ — reset.css will be picked up automatically and output as reset.min.css. No changes to build.ts needed.
7. Document usage example — no showcase directory exists currently; add a CSS comment header in the file itself showing import usage pattern, e.g.: @import '@websublime/line-theme/reset';

Risks:
- Selector scope: must only target content INSIDE line-* custom elements (slotted/light-DOM), never bare element selectors that would affect the whole document — that is normalize.css's job
- Over-resetting: aggressive resets on slotted content could surprise consumers. Keep resets minimal (margin, padding, font inheritance, box-sizing). The :where() zero specificity mitigates this since consumers can always override
- Component tag names: reset references line-* tag names that do not exist yet. This is fine — CSS selectors for non-existent elements are inert. But the file should be structured so adding new component resets later is straightforward (one section per component pattern)
- package.json exports field does not exist yet — it needs to be added as a new field in package.json

Related tests: No CSS test infrastructure exists in the theme package currently. Validation would be manual: build the package and verify reset.min.css appears in dist/ with correct content.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
REVIEW:
Acceptance: PASS — all criteria met:
  1. reset.css exists in packages/theme/src/ — YES (168 lines)
  2. Uses only :where() selectors for zero specificity — YES (every rule wrapped in :where())
  3. File is optional, consumers opt in explicitly — YES (not imported in line.css)
  4. Covers common light-DOM and slotted content resets — YES (7 sections: generic, field, form, content containers, navigation, buttons, tables)
  5. Referenced in theme package.json exports — YES ("./reset": "./dist/reset.min.css")
  6. Documented with usage example — YES (CSS comment header lines 1-13 with @import and link examples)

Findings:
- [WARNING] reset.css:23 — Section 1 uses [class*="line-"] as parent selector, which matches ANY element whose class attribute contains the substring "line-" (e.g., class="outline-primary", class="airline-logo"). Web Components have tag names (line-button, line-card) not classes. This creates false-positive matches on unrelated elements. Consider using a tag-name-based approach like [class*="line-"] -> a custom attribute selector or listing known component groups, consistent with sections 2-7 which correctly use explicit tag names. The :where() zero-specificity mitigates the blast radius, but the semantic intent is wrong.
- [WARNING] reset.css:23-41 — Section 1 (generic slotted resets) overlaps substantially with sections 4-5. For example, h1-h6/p/ul/ol resets in section 1 already cover the same elements reset in section 4 (content containers) and section 5 (navigation). If the generic section is kept, the component-specific sections for the same properties become redundant. If removed, the component-specific sections are self-contained. Either approach is fine, but having both creates maintenance burden where changes must be synced across sections.
- [SUGGESTION] reset.css:140 — Button reset targets button:not([class]) which means any button with ANY class (even class="close") skips the reset. This is a reasonable heuristic but may surprise consumers. Consider documenting this behavior in the section comment.
- [SUGGESTION] build.ts — The commit includes Biome reformatting of the entire file (collapsing multi-line arrays and function signatures to single lines). While harmless, mixing formatting changes with feature additions makes the diff noisier than necessary. Prefer separate commits for formatting vs. feature changes.
- [GOOD] reset.css:1-13 — Excellent documentation header with clear opt-in usage examples for both @import and link tag approaches.
- [GOOD] reset.css — Well-organized into 7 logical sections with clear section headers and spec references. Easy to extend with new component resets.
- [GOOD] package.json — Clean exports field addition alongside existing entries.
- [GOOD] line.css — Correctly does NOT import reset.css, preserving opt-in semantics.

Security: PASS — CSS-only change, no injection vectors, no dynamic content.
Performance: PASS — Zero-specificity selectors have negligible performance impact. File is small (168 lines, 2272 bytes minified).
Tests: PASS (with caveat) — No CSS test infrastructure exists in the theme package. Build verification (120/120 entries, reset.min.css produced) is the best available validation. No regression risk.

Verdict: NEEDS-REFACTORING — Two warnings: the [class*="line-"] selector mismatch and the redundancy between generic and component-specific sections. Neither blocks functionality (zero-specificity is a safety net), but both should be addressed for correctness and maintainability.

comments.author: Miguel Ramos
comments.text:
REFACTORING:
Findings processed: 4 (2 warnings, 2 suggestions)

FIXED:
- reset.css:23-41 — Removed section 1 (generic slotted content resets) which used [class*="line-"] attribute selector. This selector false-positively matched any element with a class containing "line-" substring (e.g., outline-primary, airline-logo). Web Components use tag names, not classes. Sections 2-6 already provide self-contained component-specific resets with explicit tag names, making the generic section both semantically incorrect and redundant.
- reset.css:140 — Added documentation comment to section 5 (button resets) explaining the button:not([class]) heuristic: buttons with any class attribute are excluded from the reset, which avoids overriding consumer-provided styling.

FALSE-POSITIVE:
- build.ts — Biome reformatting mixed with feature changes. This is valid process feedback but not a code issue. The formatting is Biome-compliant and cannot be retroactively separated without rewriting git history.

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION:
Root cause: The vita- branding persists in two source files (inspector CSS classes and localStorage key), plus docs/config references. No customElements.define calls use vita- prefix directly (they take a name parameter). The inspector element uses ui-inspector tag which BASE-SPEC says should become line-inspector (separate task P0-E4-T2), but the vita- CSS classes inside it are in scope here.

FILES (source code -- must change):
- packages/core/src/lib/ui/inspector.ts:19,30,43,48,53-55,130,142,147,149,153,156 -- CSS classes (.vita-inspector-container, .vita-inspector-info, .vita-pkg-scope, .vita-pkg-version) and HTML class attributes using these names. All are internal Shadow DOM styles, so renaming is safe with zero external impact.
- packages/core/src/lib/controllers/inspect-controller.ts:19,42 -- JSDoc comment references vita-inspector (line 19) and localStorage key 'vita-inspector' (line 42). The localStorage key is a runtime API surface -- renaming it will invalidate any existing stored values for users (acceptable for pre-1.0).

FILES (docs/config -- should update for consistency):
- .claude/agents/lit-web-components-supervisor.md:186-187 -- References vita- tag prefix and --vita- CSS prefix in naming convention section.
- .spec/BASE-SPEC.md:24,36,37,434 -- Documents the old vita-inspector localStorage key and vita- tag prefix. Some lines describe the migration itself (lines 36,37,434) so those should be updated to reflect completion.
- docs/PRODUCT-PLAN.md:50 -- Task description references vita- (this is descriptive, may leave as-is since it describes the task).
- docs/PRODUCT-REQUIREMENTS-SPECIFICATION.md:1683 -- Migration table showing vita- to line- (descriptive, should remain as documentation of the migration).
- CLAUDE.md:161 -- Branding refactor note (descriptive, may leave as-is or update after full epic completes).

NOT tag prefixes (false positives to skip):
- docs/PRODUCT-REQUIREMENTS-SPECIFICATION.md:1683 -- Migration table documenting the rename (keep vita- as historical reference).
- docs/PRODUCT-PLAN.md:50 -- Task description (keep vita- as it describes the task itself).
- CLAUDE.md:161 -- Status note about pending refactor (update after epic completes, not part of T7).

Edge cases:
- The ui-inspector custom element tag (inspector.ts:16, inspect-controller.ts:59) is NOT prefixed vita- but uses the unprefixed ui-inspector. BASE-SPEC says it should become line-inspector (P0-E4-T2). This is OUT OF SCOPE for T7 but worth noting.
- The localStorage key 'vita-inspector' is a runtime contract. Changing to 'line-inspector' is a breaking change but acceptable pre-1.0.

Approach:
1. In inspector.ts: Rename all .vita-* CSS classes to .line-* (vita-inspector-container -> line-inspector-container, vita-inspector-info -> line-inspector-info, vita-pkg-scope -> line-pkg-scope, vita-pkg-version -> line-pkg-version). Update both the CSS definitions and the HTML template class attributes.
2. In inspect-controller.ts: Change localStorage key from 'vita-inspector' to 'line-inspector'. Update the JSDoc comment.
3. In .claude/agents/lit-web-components-supervisor.md: Update naming convention from vita- to line- (lines 186-187).
